# >>> rade-ui-2: generated from the pinned RADE shared UI file (second half) by scripts/build_task_scripts.py (do not edit)
$ui.AboveBad = { param([string]$Card, $M)
  $out = @(); $tol = [math]::Max(1, (& $ui.Sc 1))
  if ([int]$M.BoxTop -lt [int]$M.LabelBottom) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' FieldRow label: its bottom is at ' + $M.LabelBottom + ', the box starts at ' + $M.BoxTop) }
  if ([math]::Abs([int]$M.BoxLeft - [int]$M.Edge) -gt $tol) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' FieldBox edge: starts at ' + $M.BoxLeft + ', the card edge is ' + $M.Edge) }
  if ([math]::Abs([int]$M.BoxW - [int]$M.TextW) -gt $tol) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' FieldBox width: ' + $M.BoxW + ', the card text is ' + $M.TextW + ' wide') }
  return $out }
# FrameBad (L1, the Administrator, 2026-11-19): the card frame. The header row starts at the frame's fixed top (so it is at
# the same place on every card of one window size), and the frame is as tall as its minimum at least, each within 1 px
# (scaled). A card that had to move up to fit (Moved) is not measured. Takes the card and @{ Top; WantTop; H; MinH; Moved };
# gives back the defect lines.
$ui.FrameBad = { param([string]$Card, $M)
  $out = @(); $tol = [math]::Max(1, (& $ui.Sc 1)); if ($M.Moved) { return $out }
  if ([math]::Abs([int]$M.Top - [int]$M.WantTop) -gt $tol) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' frame: the header row is at ' + $M.Top + ', the fixed top is ' + $M.WantTop) }
  if ([int]$M.H + $tol -lt [int]$M.MinH) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' frame: ' + $M.H + ' high, the minimum is ' + $M.MinH) }
  return $out }
# TickBad (R29b N3): the step's time or count (@{ N; Top; H }) has its vertical center within 1 px of the bar's (@{ Top; H }),
# at any scale (the tolerance is not scaled).
$ui.TickBad = { param([string]$Card, $Bar, $Tick)
  $mb = $Bar.Top + $Bar.H / 2.0; $mt = $Tick.Top + $Tick.H / 2.0
  if ([math]::Abs($mt - $mb) -le 1) { return @() }
  return @('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' StepRow ' + $Tick.N + ' midpoint: ' + $mt + ', the bar midpoint is ' + $mb) }
# ---- The self-check walk
$ui.IsCardText = { param($C) return [bool](($C -is [System.Windows.Forms.TextBox]) -and $C.ReadOnly -and -not $C.TabStop -and $ui.Wrap.ContainsKey($C)) }
# What a card text box needs, as its edit control wraps the text now (the line count it reports), else as measured.
$ui.TextNeed = { param($C)
  $w = [int](& $ui.GetWrap $C); $s = & $ui.Meas ([string]$C.Text) $C.Font $(if ($w -gt 0) { $w } else { 100000 }); $h = [int]$s.Height + (& $ui.Sc 2)
  try { $n = [int]$C.GetLineFromCharIndex([math]::Max(0, $C.Text.Length - 1)) + 1; $lh = [int][System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText('Ag', $C.Font).Height; if ($n -gt 0 -and $lh -gt 0) { $h = [math]::Max($h, $n * $lh) } } catch { $null = $_ }
  return (New-Object System.Drawing.Size($s.Width, $h)) }
# ---- UI standard v1 rules of the self-check (the Administrator, 2026-11-20; docs/ui-standard.md, each rule's check)
# The WCAG relative luminance of a color (0 to 1). Takes the color; gives back a number.
$ui.Lum = { param($C) $v = foreach ($x in @($C.R, $C.G, $C.B)) { $f = [double]$x / 255.0; if ($f -le 0.04045) { $f / 12.92 } else { [math]::Pow(($f + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4) } }; 0.2126 * $v[0] + 0.7152 * $v[1] + 0.0722 * $v[2] }
# The WCAG contrast ratio of two colors (1 to 21). Takes the two colors; gives back a number.
$ui.Ratio = { param($A, $B) $x = & $ui.Lum $A; $y = & $ui.Lum $B; ([math]::Max($x, $y) + 0.05) / ([math]::Min($x, $y) + 0.05) }
# B1 (fixed sizes) for one button with an edge: no AutoSize, a size of the set, and a label that fits. Takes the card,
# the button's name and the button; gives back the defect lines.
$ui.BtnBad = { param([string]$Card, [string]$Name, $B)
  $out = @(); $ws = @($ui.Z.CompactW, $ui.Z.ActionW, $ui.Z.WideW | ForEach-Object { & $ui.Sc $_ }); $hs = @($ui.Z.CompactH, $ui.Z.ActionH | ForEach-Object { & $ui.Sc $_ })
  if ($B.AutoSize) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' ' + $Name + ' button: AutoSize is on (B1: fixed sizes)') }
  if ($ws -notcontains [int]$B.Width -or $hs -notcontains [int]$B.Height) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' ' + $Name + ' button: ' + $B.Width + 'x' + $B.Height + ' is not a size of the set (B1)') }
  $need = [int][System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText([string]$B.Text, $B.Font).Width + (& $ui.Sc 4)
  if ($B.Text -and $need -gt [int]$B.Width) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' ' + $Name + ' button text cut: needs ' + $need + ' has ' + $B.Width + ' (B1)') }
  return $out }
# B3, B4, B5 for the card's action row: at most one primary button, and it is the last one; at most 3 others ("Back (Esc)"
# is the Back pattern, not counted). Takes the card and the kinds of the shown buttons in row order; gives back the lines.
$ui.RowRuleBad = { param([string]$Card, $Kinds)
  $out = @(); $ks = @($Kinds); $main = @(for ($k = 0; $k -lt $ks.Count; $k++) { if ([string]$ks[$k] -eq 'primary') { $k } })
  if ($main.Count -gt 1) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' buttons: ' + $main.Count + ' primary buttons, the rule is one (B4)') }
  if ($main.Count -eq 1 -and $main[0] -ne $ks.Count - 1) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' buttons: the primary button is number ' + ($main[0] + 1) + ' of ' + $ks.Count + ', the rule is last (B3)') }
  if ($ks.Count - $main.Count -gt 3) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' buttons: ' + ($ks.Count - $main.Count) + ' buttons beside the primary, the rule is 3 at most (B5)') }
  return $out }
# Inventory (RADE_INVENTORY = a file path; the Windows job): one JSON line for each control the self-check walks, with
# the card, the scale, the kind, the screen box, the colors and the accessible name (docs/ui-standard.md "Proof").
$ui.InvFile = [string]$env:RADE_INVENTORY
# Writes the inventory line of one control. Takes the card, the control and its screen box.
$ui.InvLine = { param([string]$Card, $C, $R)
  try { $o = [ordered]@{ card = $Card; scale = [int][math]::Round($ui.Dpi / 96.0 * 100); high = [bool]$ui.High; kind = $C.GetType().Name; name = (& $ui.NameOf $C)
      x = [int]$R.Left; y = [int]$R.Top; w = [int]$R.Width; h = [int]$R.Height; fore = '#{0:X6}' -f ($C.ForeColor.ToArgb() -band 0xFFFFFF); back = '#{0:X6}' -f ($C.BackColor.ToArgb() -band 0xFFFFFF)
      access = [string]$C.AccessibleName; button = [string]$ui.Kinds[$C] }
    Add-Content -LiteralPath $ui.InvFile -Value (ConvertTo-Json $o -Compress) -Encoding UTF8 -ErrorAction Stop } catch { $null = $_ } }   # the inventory is a test aid: never stop the check
$ui.Check = {
  if (-not $ui.LayOn -or -not $ui.View) { return }
  if ($ui.Picked -and (Test-Deploy) -and $env:RADE_LAYOUT -ne '1') { return }   # a deploy does not run it, also when the paste has a test application
  $card = $(if ($ui.RecOn) { 'record' } else { [string]$ui.View })
  try {
    if (-not $ui.Form.Visible -or [string]$ui.Form.WindowState -eq 'Minimized') { return }
    # One check for each card at each window size (R28: the check runs again after a resize).
    $key = $card + '|' + $ui.View + '|' + $ui.Sent.Text + '|' + $ui.Kick.Text; $ui.LayCards[$key] = 1
    $key += '|' + $ui.Form.ClientSize.Width + 'x' + $ui.Form.ClientSize.Height; if ($ui.LaySeen.ContainsKey($key)) { return }; $ui.LaySeen[$key] = 1
    if ($ui.Scrolls -and -not $ui.RecOn) { $ui.LayScroll[$card] = 1 }
    $todo = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $todo.Push(@($ui.Form, $ui.Form.RectangleToScreen($ui.Form.ClientRectangle), $false))
    while ($todo.Count) {
      $it = $todo.Pop(); $par = $it[0]; $clip = $it[1]; $scroll = $it[2]
      $kids = @($par.Controls | Where-Object { $_.Visible })
      for ($i = 0; $i -lt $kids.Count; $i++) {
        $c = $kids[$i]; $r = $c.RectangleToScreen($c.ClientRectangle); if ($r.Width -le 0 -or $r.Height -le 0) { continue }
        if ($ui.InvFile) { & $ui.InvLine $card $c $r }
        if ($c.CanSelect -and $c.TabStop -and -not [string]$c.AccessibleName) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ': no accessible name') }
        if ($ui.Boxes -contains $c -and [int]$c.Height + 1 -lt (& $ui.Sc $ui.Z.CompactH)) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' box: ' + $c.Height + ' high, the rule is ' + (& $ui.Sc $ui.Z.CompactH) + ' (B1; R36: a frame that did not scale cut its line at 150 %)') }
        if ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.Button] -and [int]$c.FlatAppearance.BorderSize -gt 0 -and $ui.BtnKind.ContainsKey($c)) { foreach ($l in @(& $ui.BtnBad $card (& $ui.NameOf $c) $c)) { $ui.LayBad.Add([string]$l) } }
        if ($c.Text -and $c.Enabled -and ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.Label] -or $c -is [System.Windows.Forms.ButtonBase] -or (& $ui.IsCardText $c))) {   # B10: text at least 4.5:1 on its own background
          $cr = & $ui.Ratio $c.ForeColor $c.BackColor; if ($cr -lt 4.5) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' contrast: ' + [math]::Round($cr, 2) + ':1, the rule is 4.5:1 (B10)') } }
        if (-not $scroll -and -not $clip.Contains($r)) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' cut: needs ' + $r.Width + 'x' + $r.Height + ' at ' + ($r.Left - $clip.Left) + ',' + ($r.Top - $clip.Top) + ' in ' + $clip.Width + 'x' + $clip.Height) }
        if ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.Label] -and $c.AutoSize -and $c.MaximumSize.Width -gt 0 -and $c.Text) { $wb = & $ui.WordBad $card (& $ui.NameOf $c) ([string]$c.Text) $c.Font $c.MaximumSize.Width; if ($wb) { $ui.LayBad.Add($wb) } }
        if (& $ui.IsCardText $c) {   # card text boxes are measured as labels are: a word wider than the line, and text that needs more room than the box has
          if ([int](& $ui.GetWrap $c) -gt 0 -and $c.Text) { $wb = & $ui.WordBad $card (& $ui.NameOf $c) ([string]$c.Text) $c.Font ([int](& $ui.GetWrap $c)); if ($wb) { $ui.LayBad.Add($wb) } }
          $nd = & $ui.TextNeed $c; if ($c.Text -and ($nd.Height -gt $c.ClientSize.Height + 1 -or $nd.Width -gt $c.ClientSize.Width + 1)) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' text: needs ' + $nd.Width + 'x' + $nd.Height + ' has ' + $c.ClientSize.Width + 'x' + $c.ClientSize.Height) }
          $lh1 = [int][System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText('Ag', $c.Font).Height; if ($c.Text -and -not $ui.Hold.ContainsKey($c) -and $c.ClientSize.Height -gt $nd.Height + $lh1) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' dead space: has ' + $c.ClientSize.Height + ' high, the text needs ' + $nd.Height) } }   # more than one empty line under its text (a box with fixed lines keeps its room)
        if ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.CheckBox] -and $c.Text -and -not $c.AutoEllipsis) {   # a one-line check box whose text alone is wider than it is cut (the Record's step boxes before R24 fix round 3)
          $tw = [System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText([string]$c.Text, $c.Font).Width; if ($tw -gt $c.ClientSize.Width + 1) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' text cut: needs ' + $tw + ' has ' + $c.ClientSize.Width) } }
        # A cut line (R28 N9: the run card's status line was cut through its middle): a control with text is at least one line of its
        # font tall, also a label that ends with "..." by rule. A rich text box (the lines of a hand step) is as tall as its text.
        if ($c.Text -and ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.Label] -or $c -is [System.Windows.Forms.ButtonBase] -or $c -is [System.Windows.Forms.TextBoxBase])) {
          $lh = [int](& $ui.LineH $c.Font); if ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.TextBoxBase]) { $lh = [int][math]::Floor($lh * 0.8) }   # an edit control draws a line with less padding
          if ($c.ClientSize.Height + 1 -lt $lh) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' line cut: one line needs ' + $lh + ' high, has ' + $c.ClientSize.Height) } }
        if ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.RichTextBox] -and $ui.GuideNeed -and [object]::ReferenceEquals($c, $ui.Guide)) { $gn = [int](& $ui.GuideNeed); if ($gn -gt $c.ClientSize.Height + 1) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' Guide text: needs ' + $gn + ' high, has ' + $c.ClientSize.Height) } }
        $isText = ($c -is [System.Windows.Forms.Label] -or $c -is [System.Windows.Forms.ButtonBase])
        if ($isText -and $c.Text -and -not $c.AutoEllipsis -and -not $ui.BtnKind.ContainsKey($c)) {   # a label or box that ends with "..." by rule is not a defect; a button of fixed size: B1
          $want = $c.GetPreferredSize((New-Object System.Drawing.Size($c.Width, 0)))
          if ($want.Width -gt $c.Width + 1 -or $want.Height -gt $c.Height + 1) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' text: needs ' + $want.Width + 'x' + $want.Height + ' has ' + $c.Width + 'x' + $c.Height) }
        }
        for ($j = $i + 1; $j -lt $kids.Count; $j++) { if ($c.Bounds.IntersectsWith($kids[$j].Bounds)) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' ' + (& $ui.NameOf $c) + ' overlaps ' + (& $ui.NameOf $kids[$j])) } }
        $sc2 = [bool]$c.AutoScroll; if ([object]::ReferenceEquals($c, $ui.Scroll)) { $sc2 = [bool]$ui.Scrolls }   # the card's text scrolls only when $ui.Squeeze says so
        if ($c.Controls.Count) { $todo.Push(@($c, [System.Drawing.Rectangle]::Intersect($clip, $r), ($scroll -or $sc2))) }
      }
    }
    # Dead space (R28 N9: a large empty area under the run card's text): the card's text panel is as tall as its text when it does not scroll.
    if ($ui.Scroll -and $ui.Body -and -not $ui.RecOn -and -not $ui.Scrolls -and $ui.Scroll.Visible) { $dead = [int]$ui.Scroll.ClientSize.Height - [int]$ui.Body.Height; if ($dead -gt (& $ui.Sc 2)) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' Scroll dead space: ' + $dead + ' px under the text') } }
    if (-not $ui.RecOn) { foreach ($l in @(& $ui.RowRuleBad $card @($ui.B | Where-Object { $_.Visible } | ForEach-Object { [string]$ui.Kinds[$_] }))) { $ui.LayBad.Add([string]$l) } }
    foreach ($l in @(& $ui.Measure $card)) { $ui.LayBad.Add([string]$l) }
  } catch { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $card + ' the self-check stopped: ' + (ConvertTo-Masked ([string]$_.Exception.Message))) } }
# RADE shared UI file, part 2 (engine/rade_ui_text.ps1): where ink starts, the text RADE draws ink-tight, long words and
# one-line texts, shortened text, and drawing and measuring ($ui.Ink to $ui.Meas). Moved out of engine/rade_ui.ps1 on
# 2026-11-23 to keep each file at 450 lines or fewer (fleet v2 DEC 6). rade_build.py puts it into every bundle right
# after engine/rade_ui.ps1, at the same marker line; an app window that copies engine/rade_ui.ps1 copies this file after
# it, as it is. Its code runs when the window calls it (no part of engine/rade_ui.ps1 calls it while it loads).
# ASCII only (a bundle is ASCII). Needs from engine/rade_ui.ps1: $ui.Sc, $ui.Pad, $ui.C, $ui.FontDpi, $ui.Scaled, $ui.Trash.
# Network: none.
# Writes: none (it measures and draws on the window only).
# Credentials: none.
# ---- Where ink starts
$ui.Inks = @{}
$ui.Ink = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Gives how far in from a control's left edge its ink starts, in pixels (the alignment rules: docs/window-design.md "Sizes").
  .DESCRIPTION
  Measured on what Windows drew (DrawToBitmap) and kept for each control kind, font, text start and size; an estimate
  from the font size when it cannot be measured (the estimate is not kept). A button with an edge gives 0.
  .PARAMETER C
  The control.
  .OUTPUTS
  The number of pixels, as an int.
  #>
  param($C)
  if ($C -is [System.Windows.Forms.ButtonBase] -and [int]$C.FlatAppearance.BorderSize -gt 0) { return 0 }
  # R28 (the Kick fix): the control is brought to the size the layout will give it BEFORE the cache key is made. The key held
  # the width the control had before it was resized, so a text measured at one width was used for another.
  try { if ($C.AutoSize -and $C.Text) { $pz = $C.PreferredSize; if ($C.Width -ne $pz.Width -or $C.Height -ne $pz.Height) { $C.Size = $pz } } } catch { $null = $_ }
  $f = $C.Font; $k = $C.GetType().Name + '|' + $f.Name + '|' + $f.SizeInPoints + '|' + $f.Style + '|' + ([string]$C.Text).PadRight(2).Substring(0, 2) + '|' +
    $(if ($C -is [System.Windows.Forms.ButtonBase] -or $C -is [System.Windows.Forms.Panel]) { [string]$C.Width + 'x' + $C.Height } else { '' })
  if ($ui.Inks.ContainsKey($k)) { return [int]$ui.Inks[$k] }
  $v = [int][math]::Ceiling([double]$f.SizeInPoints * $ui.FontDpi / 72.0 / 6.0); $got = $false
  if (-not $C.Text -and -not ($C -is [System.Windows.Forms.Panel])) { return $v }   # nothing drawn: nothing to measure
  try { $w = [math]::Max(1, $C.Width); $h = [math]::Max(1, $C.Height); $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap($w, $h)
    try { $C.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $w, $h))); $bg = $C.BackColor; $hit = -1
      for ($x = 0; $x -lt [math]::Min($w, (& $ui.Sc 40)) -and $hit -lt 0; $x++) { for ($y = 0; $y -lt $h; $y++) { $px = $bm.GetPixel($x, $y); if ([math]::Abs($px.R - $bg.R) +
        [math]::Abs($px.G - $bg.G) + [math]::Abs($px.B - $bg.B) -gt 90) { $hit = $x; break } } }
      if ($hit -ge 0) { $v = $hit; $got = $true } } finally { $bm.Dispose() } } catch { $null = $_ }
  if ($got) { $ui.Inks[$k] = $v }; return $v }   # only a measure is kept; the estimate is tried again next time
# Sets the left margin of a control to L pixels (0 at least), only when it differs. Takes the control and the margin.
$ui.SetLeft = { param($C, [int]$L) $L = [math]::Max(0, $L); $m = $C.Margin; if ($m.Left -ne $L) { $C.Margin = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Padding($L, $m.Top, $m.Right, $m.Bottom) } }
# ---- Text that RADE draws ink-tight (L2, the Administrator, 2026-11-19: the header)
# A label keeps empty room above its capitals and under its baseline (about 5 and 7 px for the word RADE), so two labels
# can never be 9 px apart ink to ink. The word RADE and the application name are panels that draw their own text and are
# exactly as tall as the ink: from the top of the capitals to the baseline (the word) or to the bottom of a "g" (a name).
# $ui.FontInk measures those rows for a font one time: "H" and "g" drawn into a bitmap by Windows. Without a bitmap (the
# test stand-ins) it gives an estimate from the text height.
$ui.FontInks = @{}
# The first and last row and column of a bitmap that hold ink (a pixel that differs from white). Takes the bitmap; gives
# back @{ Top; Bottom; Left; Right } (Bottom and Right are one past the ink), or $null when the bitmap has no ink.
$ui.InkScan = { param($Bm)
  $t = -1; $b = -1; $l = $Bm.Width; $r = -1
  for ($y = 0; $y -lt $Bm.Height; $y++) { for ($x = 0; $x -lt $Bm.Width; $x++) { $px = $Bm.GetPixel($x, $y)
      if ((255 - $px.R) + (255 - $px.G) + (255 - $px.B) -gt 90) { if ($t -lt 0) { $t = $y }; $b = $y; if ($x -lt $l) { $l = $x }; if ($x -gt $r) { $r = $x } } } }
  if ($t -lt 0) { return $null }
  return @{ Top = $t; Bottom = $b + 1; Left = $l; Right = $r + 1 } }
# Draws a text in black on a white bitmap, as $ui.InkPaint draws it (no padding, one line), and gives back its ink box
# ($ui.InkScan), or $null when nothing can be drawn (no System.Drawing bitmap). Takes the text and the font.
$ui.InkOf = { param([string]$Text, $Font)
  try { $fl = [System.Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'Left, Top, NoPadding, NoPrefix, SingleLine'
    $sz = [System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText($Text, $Font, (New-Object System.Drawing.Size(100000, 0)), $fl)
    $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap(([math]::Max(1, [int]$sz.Width + 4)), ([math]::Max(1, [int]$sz.Height + 4)))
    try { $g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bm); $g.Clear([System.Drawing.Color]::White)
      [System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($g, $Text, $Font, (New-Object System.Drawing.Point(0, 0)), [System.Drawing.Color]::Black, [System.Drawing.Color]::White, $fl); $g.Dispose()
      return (& $ui.InkScan $bm) } finally { $bm.Dispose() } } catch { return $null } }
# The rows of a font's ink in a text cell: Top = the top of the capitals, Base = the baseline (one past the bottom of "H"),
# Bottom = one past the bottom of "g". Measured one time for each font; an estimate when it cannot be measured.
$ui.FontInk = { param($Font)
  $k = [string]$Font.Name + '|' + $Font.SizeInPoints + '|' + $Font.Style; if ($ui.FontInks.ContainsKey($k)) { return $ui.FontInks[$k] }
  $h = 18; try { $h = [int][System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText('Hg', $Font).Height } catch { $null = $_ }   # no measure: the height of the form font
  $v = @{ Top = [int][math]::Round($h * 0.27); Base = [int][math]::Round($h * 0.8); Bottom = $h }
  $a = & $ui.InkOf 'H' $Font; $d = & $ui.InkOf 'g' $Font
  if ($a -and $d) { $v = @{ Top = [int]$a.Top; Base = [int]$a.Bottom; Bottom = [int][math]::Max($a.Bottom, $d.Bottom) }; $ui.FontInks[$k] = $v }   # only a measure is kept
  return $v }
# Makes a panel that draws its own Text ink-tight. Takes the font, the color, the screen-reader name and whether the
# panel keeps room for descenders ($true: a name; $false: capitals only, the panel ends on the baseline). Gives back the
# panel; $ui.InkFit sizes it when its text changes and when the window has its scale.
$ui.InkText = { param($Font, $Color, [string]$Name, [bool]$Desc)
  $p = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel; $p.Font = $Font; $p.ForeColor = $Color; $p.BackColor = $ui.C.White; $p.Margin = (& $ui.Pad 0 0 0 0); $p.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(1, 1)
  $p.AccessibleRole = 'StaticText'; $p.AccessibleName = $Name; $p.Tag = @{ Desc = $Desc; Left = 0; MaxW = 0; Cut = $false }; $p.Visible = $false
  $p.Add_Paint({ & $ui.InkPaint $this $_.Graphics }); $p.Add_TextChanged({ & $ui.InkFit $this }); $p }
# Sizes an ink-tight panel to its text: as wide as the ink (at most Tag.MaxW when that is set: the text then ends with
# "...") and as tall as the font's ink rows. Does nothing before the window has its scale. Takes the panel.
$ui.InkFit = { param($P)
  if (-not $ui.Scaled) { return }
  try { $fi = & $ui.FontInk $P.Font; $h = $(if ($P.Tag.Desc) { $fi.Bottom } else { $fi.Base }) - $fi.Top; $w = 1; $P.Tag.Left = 0
    if ($P.Text) { $box = & $ui.InkOf ([string]$P.Text) $P.Font
      if ($box) { $P.Tag.Left = [int]$box.Left; $w = [int]$box.Right - [int]$box.Left }
      else { $w = [int][System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText([string]$P.Text, $P.Font).Width } }
    $P.Tag.Cut = ([int]$P.Tag.MaxW -gt 0 -and $w -gt [int]$P.Tag.MaxW)   # cut = the text is wider than its widest size: only then it ends with "..."
    if ($P.Tag.Cut) { $w = [int]$P.Tag.MaxW }
    $ns = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(([math]::Max(1, $w)), ([math]::Max(1, $h))); if ($P.Width -ne $ns.Width -or $P.Height -ne $ns.Height) { $P.Size = $ns }
    if ($P.Text) { $P.AccessibleName = [string]$P.Text }; $P.Invalidate() } catch { $null = $_ } }   # no size now: the next fit sizes it
# Draws the text of an ink-tight panel: moved left and up by the empty room of its text cell, so the ink starts at the
# panel's left and top edge; a text cut to its widest size (Tag.Cut) ends with "...". Takes the panel and its Graphics.
$ui.InkPaint = { param($P, $G)
  try { $G.Clear($P.BackColor); if (-not $P.Text) { return }
    $fi = & $ui.FontInk $P.Font; $l = [int]$P.Tag.Left
    # R32 (the Administrator, 2026-11-18: "RA..." at 150 %): the panel is as wide as the ink, and Windows needs the text's whole
    # cell (the ink and the last letter's side room, 1 or 2 px more at a large size) or it ends the text with "...". So a text
    # that is not cut gets room past the panel's edge (nothing is drawn there) and no "..." rule; a cut text keeps both.
    $room = $P.ClientSize.Width + $l; $fl = 'Left, Top, NoPadding, NoPrefix, SingleLine, EndEllipsis'
    if (-not $P.Tag.Cut) { $room += [int][math]::Max(8, $fi.Bottom); $fl = 'Left, Top, NoPadding, NoPrefix, SingleLine' }
    [System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($G, [string]$P.Text, $P.Font, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle((-$l), (-[int]$fi.Top), $room, ([int]$fi.Bottom + 4))), $P.ForeColor, $P.BackColor,
      [System.Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]$fl) } catch { $null = $_ } }   # drawing never stops the window
# Where the ink of a control is, measured on what Windows drew (DrawToBitmap; the first 240 px of its width): gives back
# @{ Top; Bottom; Left; Right } in the control's own pixels, or its whole box when it cannot be measured. Takes the control.
$ui.InkBox = { param($C)
  $all = @{ Top = 0; Bottom = [int]$C.Height; Left = 0; Right = [int]$C.Width }
  try { $w = [math]::Max(1, [math]::Min([int]$C.Width, (& $ui.Sc 240))); $h = [math]::Max(1, [int]$C.Height); $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap($w, $h)
    try { $C.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $w, $h))); $box = & $ui.InkScan $bm;
      if ($box) { return $box } } finally { $bm.Dispose() } } catch { $null = $_ }   # no bitmap (the test stand-ins): the whole box
  return $all }
# ---- Long words and one-line texts
# A word wider than the line (no space in it) is cut into pieces that fit, one per line: it wraps by character and is
# never clipped (R7 review). Only what the window shows changes; the report keeps the text.
# The width a label needs to show a text in one line: asked of a label that is never shown, with the same font and flags
# as the window's labels (R24 job: TextRenderer's default flags gave 3 to 9 px more than a label uses).
$ui.Probe = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label; $ui.Probe.AutoSize = $true; $ui.Probe.UseMnemonic = $false;
  $ui.Trash = @(@($ui.Trash) | Where-Object { $_ }) + @($ui.Probe)   # disposed when the window has closed
# The width a label needs to show a text in one line ($ui.Probe). Takes the text and the font; gives back pixels.
$ui.WordW = { param([string]$T, $F) try { $ui.Probe.Font = $F; $ui.Probe.Text = $T; return [int]$ui.Probe.PreferredSize.Width } catch { return [int][System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText($T,
  $F).Width } }
$ui.Most = @{}   # the widest values of each label of changing values ($ui.FixW)
# A label that shows changing values (a percent, a count, a time; $ui.Most[label] = the widest values it can show) keeps one
# size: as wide as the widest of them and one line tall, so nothing beside it moves when the value changes (the
# Administrator, 2026-11-19). A value wider than all of them still fits: the label grows for it. Does nothing before the
# window has its scale (Windows Forms would scale the size again). Takes the label; gives back nothing.
$ui.FixW = { param($L) if (-not $ui.Scaled) { return }
  try { $w = 0; foreach ($x in @(@($ui.Most[$L]) + @([string]$L.Text) | Where-Object { $_ })) { $w = [math]::Max($w, (& $ui.WordW ([string]$x) $L.Font)) }
    $ui.Probe.Font = $L.Font; $ui.Probe.Text = '0'; $h = [int]$ui.Probe.PreferredSize.Height; if ($L.AutoSize) { $L.AutoSize = $false }
    if ($L.Width -ne $w -or $L.Height -ne $h) { $L.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size($w, $h) } } catch { $null = $_ } }   # no measure: the next fit sets it
# The height of one line of text in a font, as Windows draws it (TextRenderer: on a 150 % screen it can be taller than
# what a text box gives itself; R35 "Field line cut: one line needs 32 high, has 27"). Takes the font; gives back pixels.
$ui.LineH = { param($Font) [int][System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText('Ag', $Font).Height }
$ui.BreakLong = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Cuts each word of a text that is wider than the line into pieces that fit, one per line (the comment above).
  .PARAMETER T
  The text.
  .PARAMETER F
  The font it shows in.
  .PARAMETER W
  The line width, in pixels (0 or less: the text is not changed).
  .OUTPUTS
  The text with the long words cut, as a string; the line breaks of the text are kept.
  #>
  param([string]$T, $F, [int]$W)
  if ($W -le 0 -or -not $T) { return $T }
  $parts = foreach ($ln in ($T -split '(\r?\n)')) {   # line by line; the line breaks are kept
    if ($ln -match '^\r?\n$') { $ln; continue }
    $ws = foreach ($wd in ($ln -split ' ')) {
      if ((& $ui.WordW $wd $F) -le $W) { $wd; continue }
      # by text element (M4 review): a surrogate pair or a letter with its accents is never split
      $pc = @(); $cur = ''; $en = [System.Globalization.StringInfo]::GetTextElementEnumerator($wd)
      while ($en.MoveNext()) { $ch = [string]$en.GetTextElement(); if ($cur -and (& $ui.WordW ($cur + $ch) $F) -gt $W) { $pc += $cur; $cur = '' }; $cur += $ch }
      $pc += $cur; $pc -join "`n" }
    @($ws) -join ' ' }
  return (@($parts) -join '') }
# ---- Shortened text
# A one-line text cut to fit a width with "..." at the end, measured by the control itself (M5 review: no AutoEllipsis,
# which shows a tooltip). Binary search on the number of text elements.
$ui.Shorten = { param($C, [string]$Full, [int]$W)
  $C.Text = $Full; if ($C.PreferredSize.Width -le $W) { return }
  $si = New-Object System.Globalization.StringInfo($Full); $lo = 0; $hi = $si.LengthInTextElements
  while ($lo -lt $hi) { $mid = [int][math]::Ceiling(($lo + $hi) / 2.0); $C.Text = $si.SubstringByTextElements(0, $mid).TrimEnd() + '...';
    if ($C.PreferredSize.Width -le $W) { $lo = $mid } else { $hi = $mid - 1 } }
  $C.Text = $(if ($lo -gt 0) { $si.SubstringByTextElements(0, $lo).TrimEnd() } else { '' }) + '...' }
# Cuts a text to N lines with "..." (the help below).
$ui.FitLines = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Cuts a text to at most N lines at a width, with "..." at its end when it is cut (the Administrator, 2026-11-19).
  .DESCRIPTION
  Measured as a card text box wraps ($ui.Meas). Binary search on the number of text elements, so a letter with its accents
  is never split. The text is not changed when it fits.
  .PARAMETER T
  The text.
  .PARAMETER F
  The font it shows in.
  .PARAMETER W
  The wrap width, in pixels.
  .PARAMETER N
  The most lines it may take.
  .OUTPUTS
  The text that fits, as a string.
  #>
  param([string]$T, $F, [int]$W, [int]$N)
  if (-not $T -or $W -le 0 -or $N -le 0) { return $T }
  $most = $N * (& $ui.Meas 'Ag' $F 100000).Height
  if ((& $ui.Meas $T $F $W).Height -le $most) { return $T }
  $si = New-Object System.Globalization.StringInfo($T); $lo = 0; $hi = $si.LengthInTextElements
  while ($lo -lt $hi) { $mid = [int][math]::Ceiling(($lo + $hi) / 2.0); $x = $si.SubstringByTextElements(0, $mid).TrimEnd() + '...';
    if ((& $ui.Meas $x $F $W).Height -le $most) { $lo = $mid } else { $hi = $mid - 1 } }
  return ($(if ($lo -gt 0) { $si.SubstringByTextElements(0, $lo).TrimEnd() } else { '' }) + '...') }
# The self-check's rule for it: a word of a text that wraps is never wider than the line the text may take (a label's
# MaximumSize, a card text box's $ui.GetWrap; else the word is cut). Not the label's own width: a wrapping label is as wide
# as its widest line by its own measure, about 1 % narrower than the probe's, so a cut piece that is the widest line would
# always seem too wide (R28 job: 591/588, 597/591, 592/588).
$ui.WordBad = { param([string]$Card, [string]$Name, [string]$Text, $F, [int]$W)
  foreach ($wd in ($Text -split '\s+')) { if ($wd) { $ww = & $ui.WordW $wd $F; if ($ww -gt $W + 1) { return ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' ' + $Name + ' text: the word "' +
    $(if ($wd -match '[\\/]') { '<a path>' } elseif ($wd.Length -gt 20) { $wd.Substring(0, 20) + '...' } else { $wd }) + '" needs ' + $ww + ', the line is ' + $W) } } }
  return $null }
# ---- Drawing and measuring
# Draws a text in a box with TextRenderer. Takes the Graphics, the text, the font, the color, the box and the flags.
$ui.Word = { param($G, [string]$Text, $Font, $Color, [int]$X, [int]$Y, [int]$W, [int]$H, [string]$Flags) [System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($G, $Text, $Font,
  (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle($X, $Y, [math]::Max(1, $W), $H)), $Color, [System.Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]$Flags) }
# The size of a text that wraps at a width (the real font; docs/window-design.md "Text lengths").
$ui.Meas = { param([string]$Text, $Font, [int]$W) [System.Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText($Text, $Font, (New-Object System.Drawing.Size([math]::Max(1, $W), 0)),
  [System.Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'WordBreak, NoPrefix, TextBoxControl') }
# <<< rade-ui-2
# ---- High contrast (R31 W2; R30b check 10: the window kept its own colors when a contrast theme came on)
# With Windows high contrast on, the window paints with the system colors of the theme instead of its own palette.
# The role of each color: backgrounds become Window, text and lines WindowText, muted text GrayText, the action
# Highlight, a button that is not available ButtonFace. The rail turns round: navy (its background) becomes WindowText
# and its light text Window, so it stays readable. One table serves $pc and $ui.C: a hashtable key ignores case, and
# each name the two share (navy, ink, track, white) has one role in both. Yellow fills become Window: dark text on the
# theme's Highlight color can be hard to read.
$ui.HcRole = @{ ink = 'WindowText'; muted = 'GrayText'; surface = 'Window'; line = 'WindowText'; navy = 'WindowText'; onPrimaryMuted = 'Window'
  accentFill = 'Window'; primary = 'Highlight'; track = 'GrayText'; redTint = 'Window'; amberTint = 'Window'; greenTint = 'Window'; white = 'Window'
  blue = 'Highlight'; yellow = 'Window'; green = 'WindowText'; greenInk = 'WindowText'; red = 'WindowText'; gray = 'GrayText'; edge = 'WindowText'
  hair = 'GrayText'; off = 'ButtonFace'; offInk = 'GrayText' }
# R11 (engine-v29: new tokens Face, FaceInk, OnBlue, Link, Focus): each RADE token this table does not name takes the
# system color RADE gives its role ($ui.Tok, 4th value), so no button loses its label with high contrast on.
foreach ($k in @($ui.Tok.Keys)) { if (-not $ui.HcRole.ContainsKey($k)) { $ui.HcRole[$k] = [string]$ui.Tok[$k][3] } }
function Select-T22Color([bool]$High, [hashtable]$Own, [hashtable]$Role) {
  # The colors to paint with: a new table with the keys of $Own. $High false: the colors of $Own. $High true: for each
  # key the system color its role names in $Role (a key with no role gets WindowText, so no text is lost). $Own is not
  # changed. The measure part checks this choice without switching the Windows theme (tests/ps/Test-T22Layout.ps1).
  $out = @{}
  foreach ($k in @($Own.Keys)) {
    if ($High) { $r = [string]$Role[$k]; if (-not $r) { $r = 'WindowText' }; $out[$k] = [System.Drawing.SystemColors]::$r }
    else { $out[$k] = $Own[$k] } }
  return $out
}
# The window's own colors, kept before any change, and whether the system colors are in use.
# R11 (engine-v29 fills $ui.C with system colors when the window opens with high contrast on): the own colors of the
# RADE tokens come from $ui.Tok, never from the live $ui.C.
$ui.OwnPc = $pc.Clone(); $ui.OwnC = $ui.C.Clone(); $ui.High = $false
foreach ($k in @($ui.Tok.Keys)) { $t = $ui.Tok[$k]; $ui.OwnC[$k] = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb([int]$t[0], [int]$t[1], [int]$t[2]) }
# Puts the colors for $High into $pc and $ui.C in place (every builder and every paint handler reads them there).
$ui.UseColors = { param([bool]$High)
  $a = Select-T22Color $High $ui.OwnPc $ui.HcRole; foreach ($k in @($a.Keys)) { $pc[$k] = $a[$k] }
  $b = Select-T22Color $High $ui.OwnC $ui.HcRole; foreach ($k in @($b.Keys)) { $ui.C[$k] = $b[$k] }
  $ui.High = $High }
'@ }

# A size at 100 % in screen pixels (the RADE scale).
$wn.Sc = { param([double]$Px) & $ui.Sc $Px }
# The height of one line of text in font $F, in pixels (as a card text box spaces its lines).
$wn.LineH = { param($F) return [int][Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText('Ag', $F).Height }
# The top of control $C in the pixels of the page (the sum of the tops up to the page), from the layout alone: no handle needed.
$wn.PageTop = { param($C) $y = 0; while ($C -and -not [object]::ReferenceEquals($C, $page)) { $y += $C.Top; $C = $C.Parent }; return $y }
# The vertical middle of the first text line of control $C, in page pixels (R6, D1 to D3). A card text box draws its
# first line at its top: top + one line / 2. A chip or a crumb link draws its text in its vertical middle: top + height / 2.
$wn.TextMid = { param($C)
  if ($C -is [Windows.Forms.TextBox]) { return ((& $wn.PageTop $C) + (& $wn.LineH $C.Font) / 2.0) }
  return ((& $wn.PageTop $C) + $C.Height / 2.0) }
$wn.ChipTops = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R7 (R32 W3): the one rule for every chip beside text: the chip's middle is the middle of the first text line.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The text keeps its top; the chip's top is the line's middle less half the chip, rounded to a pixel (so the two
  middles differ by half a pixel at most, at any scale). When that top would be above 0 (a chip taller than the
  line, with the text at the top), both move down by the same amount: the chip starts at 0 and the text lower.
  The tops are relative to the same parent top (a panel placed by hand, or the margins of a flow row).
  .PARAMETER ChipH
  The chip's height in pixels.
  .PARAMETER Font
  The font of the text beside the chip ($wn.LineH gives its line height).
  .PARAMETER TextTop
  Where the text would start, in pixels.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Chip = the chip's top; Text = the text's top }.
  #>
  param([int]$ChipH, $Font, [int]$TextTop)
  $c = [int][math]::Round($TextTop + (& $wn.LineH $Font) / 2.0 - $ChipH / 2.0); $t = $TextTop
  if ($c -lt 0) { $t = $TextTop - $c; $c = 0 }
  return @{ Chip = $c; Text = $t } }
# Keeps chip $Chip and the text box $Text beside it for the measure part and the layout self-check (R7 W3); $Kind
# names the block (check, list, rows, chips, notice).
$wn.KeepChip = { param($Chip, $Text, [string]$Kind) $wn.ChipRows += @{ Chip = $Chip; Text = $Text; Kind = $Kind } }

$wn.Blocks.check = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  A check result: a green chip, its text and (R30 V3: only when it has something to open) its link.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R6 (R31b D3): the chip's vertical middle is the middle of the first line of the text (within half a pixel, at any
  scale). The chip is taller than a line, so the text starts lower by the difference and the chip sits at the top.
  R7 (W3): the same rule as every other chip beside text ($wn.ChipTops); each chip and its text are kept in
  $wn.ChipRows ($wn.KeepChip) for the measure part and the layout self-check.
  .PARAMETER Parent
  The card that gets the check.
  .PARAMETER b
  The block: Chip (the chip's word), Text, Findings and Link.
  .PARAMETER W
  The width of the check row.
  #>
  param($Parent, $b, [int]$W)
  $p = & $wn.Panel $W 8
  $cp = & $wn.Chip 'ok' $b.Chip $ui.C.White; [void]$p.Controls.Add($cp)
  $x = $cp.Width + (& $wn.Sc 10)
  $t = & $wn.Txt $p $b.Text $ui.F.Body $ui.C.Ink 0 ($W - $x) 'Check result' $null
  $tops = & $wn.ChipTops $cp.Height $t.Font 0   # R7: the one chip rule (the chip is taller than the line: the text starts lower)
  $cp.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(0, $tops.Chip); $t.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($x, $tops.Text)
  & $wn.KeepChip $cp $t 'check'
  if (Test-CheckLink $b) { $l = & $wn.Link $b.Link; $l.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($x, ($t.Bottom + (& $wn.Sc 2))); [void]$p.Controls.Add($l) }
  & $wn.Fit $p 4; [void]$Parent.Controls.Add($p) }

$wn.Blocks.rows = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Label and value rows with a line between them; the value is a chip when the row names a chip kind.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R7 (R32 W3): a chip's middle is the middle of its label's first line ($wn.ChipTops; it was about 2 px lower), and
  the chip is kept with its label in $wn.ChipRows ($wn.KeepChip).
  .PARAMETER Parent
  The card that gets the rows.
  .PARAMETER b
  The block: Rows, each @(label, value, chip kind or '').
  .PARAMETER W
  The width of the rows.
  #>
  param($Parent, $b, [int]$W)
  $first = $true
  foreach ($r in @($b.Rows)) {
    if (-not $first) { & $wn.Rule $Parent $W 0 }
    $p = & $wn.Panel $W 0
    $lw = [int]($W * 0.5); $vw = $W - $lw - (& $wn.Sc 16)

      $a.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(0, $tops.Text); $v.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(($W - $v.Width), $tops.Chip); [void]$p.Controls.Add($v); & $wn.KeepChip $v $a 'rows' }
    else { $v = & $wn.Txt $p $r[1] $ui.F.SmallB $ui.C.Ink 0 $vw 'Value' $null; $v.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(($W - $v.Width), (& $wn.Sc 8)) }
    & $wn.Fit $p 8; [void]$Parent.Controls.Add($p); $first = $false } }
$wn.ListRow = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  One row of a list: an optional chip, a title, up to two gray lines and an optional compact button at the right.
  .PARAMETER Parent
  The card that gets the row.
  .PARAMETER It
  The list item: Chip, Title, Sub, Detail, Btn.
  .PARAMETER W
  The width of the row.
  .PARAMETER Tx
  Where the text starts (the width of the widest chip of the list and a gap; 0 without chips).
  #>
  param($Parent, $It, [int]$W, [int]$Tx)
  $p = & $wn.Panel $W 0
  $bw = 0; $btn = $null
  # R11 (UI standard v1, B1): the button keeps the fixed size RADE gives it (compact 96 x 30, or 160 x 30 for a longer label)
  if ($It.Btn) { $btn = & $wn.Button $It.Btn 'compact'; $bw = [int]$btn.Width }
  $tw = $W - $Tx - $bw - (& $wn.Sc 16) - (& $wn.Sc 8)
  $y = & $wn.Sc 8
  $t1 = & $wn.Txt $p $It.Title $ui.F.SmallB $ui.C.Ink 0 $tw 'Item' $null
  if ($It.Chip) {   # R7 (W3): the chip's middle is the title's first-line middle ($wn.ChipTops), not 7 px lower
    $cp = & $wn.Chip $It.Chip[0] $It.Chip[1] $ui.C.White; $tops = & $wn.ChipTops $cp.Height $t1.Font $y; $y = $tops.Text
    $cp.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(0, $tops.Chip); [void]$p.Controls.Add($cp); & $wn.KeepChip $cp $t1 'list' }
  $t1.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($Tx, $y); $y = $t1.Bottom + (& $wn.Sc 2)
  if ($It.Sub) { $t2 = & $wn.Txt $p $It.Sub $ui.F.Small $ui.C.Gray 0 $tw 'Item detail' $null; $t2.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($Tx, $y); $y = $t2.Bottom + (& $wn.Sc 2) }
  if ($It.Detail) { $t3 = & $wn.Txt $p $It.Detail $ui.F.Small $ui.C.Gray 0 $tw 'Item detail' $null; $t3.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($Tx, $y); $y = $t3.Bottom }
  if ($btn) {
    $btn.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(($W - $bw - (& $wn.Sc 4)), [math]::Max((& $wn.Sc 6), [int](($y + (& $wn.Sc 8) - $btn.Height) / 2))); [void]$p.Controls.Add($btn) }
  & $wn.Fit $p 8; [void]$Parent.Controls.Add($p) }
# A list of rows with a line between them; the texts of all rows start after the widest chip.
$wn.Blocks.list = { param($Parent, $b, [int]$W)

# R12 (R38 finding 2, UI standard B1): a one-line text box drawn by Windows is as high as its font (39 px at 150 %);
# the rule is the compact height ($ui.Z.CompactH, 45 px at 150 %). The box goes without its own border into a white
# frame of that height, in the middle; the frame is the box for the focus ring and the self-check ($ui.Boxes,
# $ui.Ring: a box that contains the focus). Takes the text box and the frame width; returns the frame.
$wn.BoxFrame = { param($Tb, [int]$W)
  $h = [math]::Max((& $ui.Sc $ui.Z.CompactH), [int]$Tb.PreferredHeight + (& $wn.Sc 8)); $pad = & $wn.Sc 8
  $fr = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel; $fr.BackColor = $ui.C.White; $fr.BorderStyle = 'FixedSingle'; $fr.Size = [Drawing.Size]::new($W, $h)
  $fr.Margin = $Tb.Margin; $Tb.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 0 0 0; $Tb.BorderStyle = 'None'; $Tb.Width = $W - 2 * $pad - 2
  $Tb.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($pad, [int][math]::Max(0, ($h - 2 - $Tb.Height) / 2)); [void]$fr.Controls.Add($Tb)
  $fr.Add_Click({ [void]$this.Controls[0].Focus() }); $ui.Boxes = @($ui.Boxes) + @($fr)
  # The ring is drawn by the frame's parent ($ui.Ring); $ui.Cue repaints only the box's own parent (the frame), as RADE's frame does (engine 03-card.ps1)
  $Tb.Add_GotFocus({ try { $this.Parent.Parent.Invalidate() } catch { $null = $_ } }); $Tb.Add_LostFocus({ try { $this.Parent.Parent.Invalidate() } catch { $null = $_ } })
  return $fr }

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  90-161.Z Task 22 r15, part "grid": the grids of the PFM window (Who Has It Now, All Actions, Wave 1 answers): their
  size, their columns that always fit the grid's width, their painted cells, the filter and the row that opens a card.
.DESCRIPTION
  A grid is a read-only DataGridView with no lines but a thin rule under each row. Each cell is painted here by its
  column kind: pub (the number as a link, the title beside or under it), with and bold (semibold), chip (a status
  chip) and plain. Double-click or Enter on a row opens its card.
  R6 (R31b D4): the titles of a pub column start in one column: after the widest number of all the grid's rows and a
  fixed gap, when every title fits there, else every title goes under its number. Each painted pub cell is kept in
  the grid's Tag.Drawn for the measure part and the layout self-check.
  R7 (R32 W1): the pub column is never narrower than its widest number, title and head plus the cell padding
  ($wn.PubMin, $wn.GridCols), so no number is cut with dots and the head reads PUBLICATION; a grid with a pub column has
  rows 2 lines high at least ($wn.GridHeight); each painted pub cell and the pub head keep what they needed and had.
  R8 (R35 W7, R34 open point 5): no column head is shortened with dots in a narrow grid: every column keeps at least
  the width of its head ($wn.HeadMin, $wn.GridCols), and every painted head keeps what it needed and had (Tag.Heads)
  for the measure part and the layout self-check.
  R11 (R38; PFM 20 Nov 26: R37 All Actions, the status chips "Due 20 Nov 26" touched the scroll bar): a column's width comes from its
  widest value ($wn.ValueMin: the measured text, a chip with its own padding, plus the cell padding); a chip column never
  shrinks below its chip ($wn.GridCols, $wn.FitGrid), a short column ("Weekdays in step" holds 1 or 2 digits) is as wide
  as its values or its head, and a head marked HW wraps to 2 lines ($wn.HeadWrap, $wn.HeadMin, $wn.GridHeight). Each grid
  can say where its content ends ($wn.GridEdges), so the layout self-check ($wn.EdgeCheck) fails a chip or text that
  ends closer to the grid's right edge than the vertical scroll bar is wide.
  R15 (R42 T1; R41 finding 4: at 1920 x 1094 and 150 % 3 Status chips ended under the 26 px bar): the column plan is pure
  arithmetic ($wn.ColPlan, run by tests/check_t22_r15.py) and keeps the scroll bar room; the grid fit ($wn.FitGrid) works
  on the column minimums against that room, so a grid that fits keeps its chip (r14 took the chip under the bar).
  Inputs: $ui, $wn, $pc, $mid, $GridQueue. Outputs: the $wn members below; nothing is read or saved.
  Run: not alone; 90161Z-T22-pfm-window-r15.ps1 dot-sources it from its own folder inside its try block.
  Network: none.
  Writes: none.
  Credentials: none.
#>
# Puts $Rows into grid $G, one value per column (Since: the date and the age when the column is wide, else the age).
$wn.GridFill = { param($G, $Rows)
  $G.Rows.Clear(); $G.Tag.Shown = @($Rows)
  foreach ($r in @($Rows)) {
    $vals = @(foreach ($c in $G.Tag.Cols) { & $wn.CellText $c $r })
    [void]$G.Rows.Add([object[]]$vals) } }
# The text of row $R in column $C (Since: the date and the age when the column is wide, else the age).
$wn.CellText = { param($C, $R)
  if ($C.K -eq 'since') { return $(if ($C.W -ge 100) { [string]$R.Since + ' ' + $mid + ' ' + [string]$R.Age } else { [string]$R.Age }) }
  return [string]$R[$C.N] }
$wn.GridHeight = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The height of a grid: all its rows, or (Fill) the room left in the window, at least 6 rows and at most all of them.
  .PARAMETER b
  The grid block: Rows, Fill.
  .PARAMETER Ctx
  The column context: Col, the column the grid is in (its height so far).
  .DESCRIPTION
  R7 (W1): a grid with a pub column has rows tall enough for 2 lines of the link font ($wn.PubLineH) and 2 px above and
  below, so a title under its number is never cut; at 100 % this is the usual 41 px.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ H = the grid height; Full = the height with every row; Hdr = the header height; Row = the row height }.
  #>
  param($b, $Ctx)
  $rows = @($b.Rows); $hdrH = & $wn.Sc 33; $rowH = & $wn.Sc 41
  # R11: a head that wraps to 2 lines (HW) needs one more line of the head font
  if (@(@($b.Cols) + @($b.ColsWide) | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.HW }).Count) { $hdrH += [int]$ui.F.SmallB.Height }
  if (@($b.Cols | Where-Object { $_.K -eq 'pub' }).Count) { $rowH = [math]::Max($rowH, 2 * (& $wn.PubLineH) + (& $wn.Sc 4) + 1) }
  $full = $hdrH + $rowH * $rows.Count + 2; $h = $full
  if ($b.Fill) {
    $used = 0; try { $used = [int]$Ctx.Col.PreferredSize.Height } catch { $null = $_ }
    $avail = $wn.MainH - $wn.HeadH - $used - (& $wn.Sc 70); $h = [int][math]::Min($full, [math]::Max($avail, $hdrH + 6 * $rowH)) }
  return @{ H = $h; Full = $full; Hdr = $hdrH; Row = $rowH } }
$wn.GridNew = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  A new empty grid with the window's look: read-only, whole-row selection, no lines, wrapped cells, white header.
  .PARAMETER Name
  The accessible name of the grid.
  .PARAMETER W
  The grid width.
  .PARAMETER Hs
  The heights from $wn.GridHeight.
  .OUTPUTS
  The DataGridView.
  #>
  param([string]$Name, [int]$W, $Hs)
  $g = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.DataGridView
  $g.AccessibleName = $Name; $g.Size = [Drawing.Size]::new($W, $Hs.H); $g.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 (& $wn.Sc 8) 0 0
  $g.AllowUserToAddRows = $false; $g.AllowUserToDeleteRows = $false; $g.AllowUserToResizeRows = $false; $g.AllowUserToResizeColumns = $false
  $g.ReadOnly = $true; $g.RowHeadersVisible = $false; $g.MultiSelect = $false; $g.SelectionMode = 'FullRowSelect'; $g.EnableHeadersVisualStyles = $false
  $g.ColumnHeadersHeightSizeMode = 'DisableResizing'; $g.ColumnHeadersHeight = $Hs.Hdr; $g.RowTemplate.Height = $Hs.Row
  $g.CellBorderStyle = 'None'; $g.ColumnHeadersBorderStyle = 'None'; $g.BorderStyle = 'None'; $g.BackgroundColor = $ui.C.White; $g.GridColor = $pc.line
  $g.AutoSizeColumnsMode='Fill'; $g.ScrollBars = 'Vertical'; $g.DefaultCellStyle.WrapMode = 'True'; $g.AutoSizeRowsMode = 'AllCells'; $g.RowTemplate.MinimumHeight = $Hs.Row
  $g.DefaultCellStyle.Padding = & $ui.Pad (& $ui.Sc 10) (& $ui.Sc 8) (& $ui.Sc 10) (& $ui.Sc 8)
  $g.DefaultCellStyle.Font = $ui.F.Small; $g.DefaultCellStyle.ForeColor = $ui.C.Ink; $g.DefaultCellStyle.BackColor = $ui.C.White
  $g.DefaultCellStyle.SelectionBackColor = $pc.surface; $g.DefaultCellStyle.SelectionForeColor = $ui.C.Ink
  $g.ColumnHeadersDefaultCellStyle.BackColor = $ui.C.White; $g.ColumnHeadersDefaultCellStyle.ForeColor = $pc.muted
  $g.ColumnHeadersDefaultCellStyle.Font = $ui.F.SmallB; $g.ColumnHeadersDefaultCellStyle.SelectionBackColor = $ui.C.White
  return $g }
$wn.ColPlan = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R15: the column plan of a grid, pure arithmetic: the smallest width and the fill weight of each column (R28 finding 4).
  .DESCRIPTION
  Every column fills: a column keeps at most its own width as its minimum, and all minimums together never exceed the
  room the grid has: the grid width less the vertical scroll bar ($wn.BarW; R15: kept in every grid, whether the bar
  shows or not) and 2 px, so the visible columns never end under the bar.
  R7 (R32 W1): a pub column keeps its whole minimum, $PubMin (its widest number, title and head plus the cell padding),
  so a number is never cut; the other columns share what is left (their text wraps).
  R8 (R35 W7): each other column keeps at least its head ($wn.HeadMin) when all heads fit: it wants the larger of its
  own width and its head; when all wants do not fit, each gets its head and the rest is shared by what it wanted more.
  Only when the heads alone do not fit do the columns shrink by one factor as before (the self-check names a cut head).
  R11 (R38): a column that is not the pub column wants the narrower of its declared width and its widest value, so a
  short column gives its room away; a chip column wants its widest chip (never less) and keeps it whole when the room is
  short, like the pub column; the fill weight of a column is the width it wants.
  .PARAMETER Cols
  The column list: N, W (0 = takes the rest), K, H.
  .PARAMETER W
  The grid width.
  .PARAMETER Scroll
  The width of the vertical scroll bar when the grid scrolls, else 0 (the fill weight of the column that takes the rest).
  .PARAMETER PubMin
  The smallest width of a pub column ($wn.PubMin), or 0.
  .PARAMETER Rows
  R11: all the rows of the grid, to measure each column's widest value ($wn.ValueMin); none: the declared widths.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Min = the smallest width by column name, in column order; Weight = the fill weight by name; Room = the room the
  minimums share; Reserve = the grid width less that room ($wn.FitGrid keeps it); ChipKept = $true or $false when the grid has a chip column (its chip kept whole), else $null }.
  #>
  param($Cols, [int]$W, [int]$Scroll, [int]$PubMin, $Rows = @())
  # R15: the room for the scroll bar is kept in every grid (r14: only with a pub column). ps51 W7 (96 dpi, narrowest page):
  # a grid with no pub column and no bar showing gives that room to its heads when only then they all fit (as r14).
  $bar = [math]::Max($Scroll, [int](& $wn.BarW)); $heads = 0; foreach ($c in $Cols) { $heads += [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c) }
  if ($PubMin -le 0 -and $Scroll -eq 0 -and $heads -gt $W - $bar - 2 -and $heads -le $W - 2) { $bar = 0 }
  $fixed = 0; $keep = 0; $rest = 0; $n = @($Cols).Count; $avail = $W - $bar - 2; $kept = $null
  $pubOwn = [math]::Max(2, [math]::Min([math]::Max((& $wn.Sc 60), $PubMin), $avail - 2 * ($n - 1)))   # a pub column never leaves less than 2 px a column
  $own = @{}; $hard = @{}; $spare = & $wn.HeadSpare $Cols $avail $PubMin $pubOwn; foreach ($c in $Cols) {   # R11: a chip is kept only while the heads fit
    $isPub = ($c.K -eq 'pub' -and $PubMin -gt 0); $vm = $(if (@($Rows).Count) { [int](& $wn.ValueMin $c $Rows) } else { 0 })
    $chipKeep = ($c.K -eq 'chip' -and $vm -gt 0 -and ($vm - [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)) -le $spare)   # Tag.ChipKept: the edge check judges only a kept chip
    if ($c.K -eq 'chip') { $kept = $chipKeep; if ($chipKeep) { $spare -= [math]::Max(0, $vm - [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)) } }
    $hard[[string]$c.N] = ($isPub -or $chipKeep)
    $o = $(if ($isPub) { $pubOwn } elseif ($chipKeep) { [math]::Max($vm, [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)) } elseif ($c.W -eq 0) { & $wn.Sc 60 }
      elseif ($vm -gt 0) { [math]::Min((& $wn.Sc $c.W), $vm) } else { & $wn.Sc $c.W }); $own[[string]$c.N] = $o
    if ($c.W -ne 0) { $fixed += $o }; if ($hard[[string]$c.N]) { $keep += $o } else { $rest += $o } }
  $k = $(if ($rest -gt 0 -and $keep + $rest -gt $avail) { [math]::Max(0.0, [double]($avail - $keep) / $rest) } else { 1.0 })
  # R8 (W7): the head floor of each other column, what it wants, and the room they share ($avail less the pub column)
  $hm = @{}; $want = 0; $floor = 0; $more = 0
  foreach ($c in $Cols) { if (-not $hard[[string]$c.N]) { $f = & $wn.HeadMin $c; $hm[[string]$c.N] = $f
      $floor += $f; $want += [math]::Max($own[[string]$c.N], $f); $more += [math]::Max(0, $own[[string]$c.N] - $f) } }
  $pool = $avail - $keep
  $mins = [ordered]@{}; $wts = @{}
  foreach ($c in $Cols) {
    $o = $own[[string]$c.N]; $f = [int]$hm[[string]$c.N]
    $mins[[string]$c.N] = [int]$(if ($hard[[string]$c.N]) { $o } elseif ($want -le $pool) { [math]::Max($o, $f) }
      elseif ($floor -le $pool) { $f + $(if ($more -gt 0) { [int][math]::Floor(($pool - $floor) * [math]::Max(0, $o - $f) / [double]$more) } else { 0 }) }
      else { [math]::Max(2, [int][math]::Floor($o * $k)) })
    $wts[[string]$c.N] = [single]$(if ($c.W -eq 0) { [math]::Max(60, $W - $fixed - $Scroll) } else { [math]::Max(1, $o) }) }
  return @{ Min = $mins; Weight = $wts; Room = $avail; Reserve = $W - $avail; ChipKept = $kept } }
# Adds the columns of the plan ($wn.ColPlan; the parameters are its own) to grid $G: each fills, with its smallest width
# and its fill weight. Gives back the column kinds by name (@{ name = kind }); $wn.ChipKept is the plan's ChipKept.
$wn.GridCols = {
  param($G, $Cols, [int]$W, [int]$Scroll, [int]$PubMin, $Rows = @())
  $plan = & $wn.ColPlan $Cols $W $Scroll $PubMin $Rows; $wn.ChipKept = $plan.ChipKept; $wn.Reserve = $plan.Reserve
  $kinds = @{}
  foreach ($c in $Cols) {
    $dc = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.DataGridViewTextBoxColumn; $dc.Name = [string]$c.N; $dc.HeaderText = $(if ($c.H) { [string]$c.H } else { [string]$c.N }); $dc.SortMode = 'NotSortable'
    $dc.AutoSizeMode='Fill'; $dc.MinimumWidth = [math]::Max(2, [int]$plan.Min[[string]$c.N]); $dc.FillWeight = $plan.Weight[[string]$c.N]
    [void]$G.Columns.Add($dc); $kinds[[string]$c.N] = [string]$c.K }
  return $kinds }
# R15: the width of a vertical scroll bar ($wn.BarW) and of the bar grid $G shows now, else 0 ($wn.BarShown), in px.
$wn.BarW = { return [int][Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VerticalScrollBarWidth }
# R15: the width of the vertical scroll bar that grid $G shows now (0 when none shows); $wn.FitGrid and $wn.EdgeCheck use it.
$wn.BarShown = { param($G) $v = @($G.Controls | Where-Object { $_ -is [Windows.Forms.VScrollBar] -and $_.Visible }); if ($v.Count) { return [int]$v[0].Width }; return 0 }
# R11 (R38; ps51 W7 at 96 dpi): the room a grid of width $Avail has above all its column heads (the pub column counts
# $PubOwn when $PubMin is above 0). $wn.GridCols keeps a status chip whole only while that room holds the chip's extra
# width, else the chip column shares the room as in r10, so a narrow window never cuts the other heads.
$wn.HeadSpare = { param($Cols, [int]$Avail, [int]$PubMin, [int]$PubOwn)
  $spare = $Avail; foreach ($c in $Cols) { $spare -= $(if ($c.K -eq 'pub' -and $PubMin -gt 0) { $PubOwn } else { [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c) }) }
  return $spare }
# R11 (R38; the PFM, 20 Nov 26: "hide Since when narrow"): the columns of a grid of width $W with each column marked Drop
# left out, last first, while the pub column's minimum ($wn.PubMin of the widths $Pw) and every other whole head do not fit
# beside the scroll bar. Wide windows keep every column.
# R12 (R38 finding 2: the Your Work grid needed 957 px and had 935 at 150 %): a chip column counts its widest chip of
# $Rows ($wn.ValueMin), not only its head, so Since leaves when the whole chips do not fit beside the other heads.
$wn.DropCols = { param($Cols, [int]$W, $Pw, $Rows = @())
  $cols = @($Cols); $avail = $W - (& $wn.BarW) - 2
  while ($true) {
    $need = [int](& $wn.PubMin $cols $Pw)
    foreach ($c in $cols) { if ($c.K -ne 'pub') { $hm = [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)
        $sb = [math]::Max((& $ui.Sc 10), [int](& $wn.BarW))   # ValueMin keeps a scroll bar right of a chip; $avail has taken it off already
        $need += $(if ($c.K -eq 'chip' -and @($Rows).Count) { [math]::Max($hm, [int](& $wn.ValueMin $c $Rows) - $sb) } else { $hm }) } }
    $drop = @($cols | Where-Object { $_.Drop }) | Select-Object -Last 1
    if ($need -le $avail -or -not $drop) { return ,$cols }
    $cols = @($cols | Where-Object { $_ -ne $drop }) } }
$wn.Grid = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  A grid block: the grid with its columns, rows, painted cells and keys; with Count, the line under it that counts the rows.
  .PARAMETER Parent
  The card that gets the grid.
  .PARAMETER b
  The grid block: Name, Rows, Cols, ColsWide (used when the window is wide and they fit), Fill, Count.
  .PARAMETER W
  The grid width.
  .PARAMETER Ctx
  The column context (for Fill).
  #>
  param($Parent, $b, [int]$W, $Ctx)
  $cols = @($b.Cols)
  if ($wn.Wide -and $b.ColsWide) { $wf = 0; foreach ($c in $b.ColsWide) { $wf += (& $wn.Sc $c.W) }; if ($wf + (& $wn.Sc 137) -le $W) { $cols = @($b.ColsWide) } }
  $rows = @($b.Rows); $pw = & $wn.PubWidths $rows; $cols = & $wn.DropCols $cols $W $pw $rows; $hs = & $wn.GridHeight $b $Ctx
  $g = & $wn.GridNew ([string]$b.Name) $W $hs
  $scroll = $(if ($hs.Full -gt $hs.H) { (& $wn.BarW) } else { 0 })
  $wn.ChipKept = $null; $kinds = & $wn.GridCols $g $cols $W $scroll (& $wn.PubMin $cols $pw) $rows
  $chipKind = @{}; foreach ($r in $rows) { if ($r.Status) { $chipKind[[string]$r.Status] = [string]$r.Kind } }
  $g.Tag = @{ Kind = $kinds; Chip = $chipKind; Cols = $cols; Shown = $rows; PubW = $pw.Num; PubT = $pw.Title; PubGap = (& $ui.Sc 6); Drawn = @{}; Head = $null
    Heads = [ordered]@{}; ChipKept = $wn.ChipKept; Reserve = $wn.Reserve }
  & $wn.GridFill $g $rows
  $g.Add_CellPainting({ param($s, $e) & $wn.PaintCell $s $e })
  $g.Add_CellDoubleClick({ param($s, $e) if ($e.RowIndex -ge 0) { & $wn.Later $s $e.RowIndex } })
  $g.Add_KeyDown({ param($s, $e) if ($e.KeyCode -eq 'Return') { $e.Handled = $true; $e.SuppressKeyPress = $true; if ($s.CurrentRow) { & $wn.Later $s $s.CurrentRow.Index } } })
  [void]$Parent.Controls.Add($g); $g.ClearSelection(); $wn.Gridsel = $g
  if ($b.Count) { $wn.CountText = [string]$b.Count; $wn.CountBox = & $wn.Txt $Parent ($b.Count -f $rows.Count) $ui.F.Small $ui.C.Gray 8 $W 'Count' $null; $wn.Gridq = $g } }
# R10 (R37; R36 finding 3: the home grid "Who has it now" columns needed 810 px, the grid had 801): after a card is laid
# out, each grid on the page whose column minimums are wider than its room gives the excess back ($wn.FitGrid). The
# layout self-check ($wn.ScrollCheck) still measures the result, so a grid that does not fit stays a defect. Gives back
# the number of grids changed.
$wn.FitGrids = {
  $n = 0; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) { if (& $wn.FitGrid $c) { $n++ } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $n }
$wn.FitGrid = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R10, R15: fits one grid (see $wn.FitGrids): lowers column minimums by the excess of the minimums over the grid's room.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R15 (R41 finding 4): the room is the client width less the plan's reserve (Tag.Reserve, $wn.ColPlan) or less the bar
  that shows now, the larger; the excess is the sum of the minimums of the visible columns less the room, so a grid
  that fits gives nothing back however its fill columns share the width. The excess comes off the columns that are not the pub column, the one with the most width above its head
  ($wn.HeadMin) first: the other columns above their heads, then the chip column above its head, then any column under
  its head (never under 2 px). When the minimums changed, or the filled columns are wider than the grid, the grid lays
  out its columns again (a 1 px size change makes the fill columns share the room again).
  R15 (R42 ps51 keep test: a later open of the Wave 1 answers card took 114 ms, 13 before): when the fit took off a bar
  that shows beyond the plan's reserve, Tag.Reserve becomes that bar and the columns keep their widths (AutoSizeMode
  None): their fill width no longer depends on the bar, and the bar no longer on the row heights the widths give, so a
  second fit, and a later open of the kept card, find nothing to do.
  .PARAMETER G
  The grid (its Tag holds the column kinds and the column list, $wn.Grid); any object with ClientSize, Width, Columns
  (Name, Visible, Width, MinimumWidth) and that Tag (tests/check_t22_r15.py gives one off Windows).
  .OUTPUTS
  $true when it changed a column or laid the grid out again, else $false.
  #>
  param($G)
  # the plan's room (Tag.Reserve), and never under a vertical bar that shows now (rows that wrap can bring one)
  $res = $(if ($null -ne $G.Tag.Reserve) { [int]$G.Tag.Reserve } else { [int](& $wn.BarW) + 2 })
  $shown = [int](& $wn.BarShown $G); $room = [int]$G.ClientSize.Width - [math]::Max($res, $shown)
  $vis = @($G.Columns | Where-Object { $_.Visible }); $mins = 0; $sum = 0
  foreach ($k in $vis) { $mins += [int]$k.MinimumWidth; $sum += [int]$k.Width }
  $excess = $mins - $room; $stale = ($sum -gt [int]$G.ClientSize.Width + 1)   # stale: the filled widths need a new layout
  if ($excess -le 0 -and -not $stale) { return $false }
  $kinds = $G.Tag.Kind; $heads = @{}; foreach ($c in @($G.Tag.Cols)) { $heads[[string]$c.N] = [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c) }
  $free = @($vis | Where-Object { [string]$kinds[$_.Name] -ne 'pub' }); $gave = 0
  foreach ($pass in 'others above head', 'above head', 'under head') {
    $set = @($free | Where-Object { $pass -ne 'others above head' -or [string]$kinds[$_.Name] -ne 'chip' })
    foreach ($k in @($set | Sort-Object { [int]$_.MinimumWidth - [int]$heads[$_.Name] } -Descending)) {
      if ($excess -le 0) { break }
      $floor = $(if ($pass -eq 'under head') { 2 } else { [math]::Max(2, [int]$heads[$k.Name]) })
      $give = [math]::Min($excess, [int]$k.MinimumWidth - $floor); if ($give -le 0) { continue }
      $k.MinimumWidth = [int]$k.MinimumWidth - $give; $excess -= $give; $gave++ } }
  if (-not $gave -and -not $stale) { return $false }   # excess, but no column could give any width back: nothing changed
  $G.Width = $G.Width - 1; $G.Width = $G.Width + 1   # the fill columns share the room again
  if ($shown -gt $res) {   # R15: the grid keeps the room of the bar that shows, and its widths stop following the bar
    $G.Tag.Reserve = $shown; foreach ($k in $vis) { $k.AutoSizeMode = 'None' } }   # (no fill and row layout again on each open)
  return $true }
# The widest number (as a link) and the widest title of the pub values ("number|title") of $Rows, in pixels, measured as
# $wn.PaintPub draws them. All rows, not only the shown ones, so a filter does not move the title column.
$wn.PubWidths = { param($Rows)
  $out = @{ Num = 0; Title = 0 }   # R15: measured by $wn.TextW (the same flags), so the column plan runs off Windows too
  foreach ($r in @($Rows)) { $pp = ([string]$r.Publication).Split('|'); if ($pp.Count -lt 2) { continue }
    $out.Num = [math]::Max($out.Num, [int](& $wn.TextW $pp[0] $ui.F.Link))
    $out.Title = [math]::Max($out.Title, [int](& $wn.TextW $pp[1] $ui.F.Small)) }
  return $out }
# The width of a one-line text $Text in font $F as the grid draws it (no padding), in pixels.
$wn.TextW = { param([string]$Text, $F)
  return [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText($Text, $F, ([Drawing.Size]::new(100000, 0)), [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'NoPadding, NoPrefix').Width }
# The head text of grid column $C as the grid draws it: its header text (H, else its name) in capitals.
$wn.HeadText = { param($C) return ($(if ($C.H) { [string]$C.H } else { [string]$C.N })).ToUpperInvariant() }
# R8 (R35 W7): the smallest width of grid column $C that shows its whole head: the head text in the head font, the cell
# padding at both sides ($wn.PaintCell) and 1 px, as $wn.PubMin does for the pub column.
# R11: a column marked HW has a head that may wrap to 2 lines: its head width is that of the wider of the 2 lines.
$wn.HeadMin = { param($C) return ((& $(if ($C.HW) { $wn.HeadWrap } else { $wn.HeadW1 }) $C) + 2 * (& $ui.Sc 10) + 1) }
# The width of the head of column $C on one line, in pixels.
$wn.HeadW1 = { param($C) return (& $wn.TextW (& $wn.HeadText $C) $ui.F.SmallB) }
# R11: the narrowest width the head of column $C shows in at most 2 lines, breaking between words: the best split into
# 2 lines, the width of its wider line; the one-line width when the head is one word.
$wn.HeadWrap = { param($C)
  $words = @((& $wn.HeadText $C) -split ' ' | Where-Object { $_ }); $best = & $wn.HeadW1 $C
  for ($i = 1; $i -lt $words.Count; $i++) {
    $a = & $wn.TextW (($words[0..($i - 1)]) -join ' ') $ui.F.SmallB; $b = & $wn.TextW (($words[$i..($words.Count - 1)]) -join ' ') $ui.F.SmallB
    $best = [math]::Min($best, [math]::Max($a, $b)) }
  return $best }
# R11 (R38): the width column $C needs for its widest value in $Rows: the text as the grid paints it (a chip: the text and
# the chip's own padding, as $wn.PaintChip draws it) plus the cell padding at both sides and 1 px (right of a chip: at least
# the width of a vertical scroll bar, so the chip never ends under it); 0 when no row has a value.
$wn.ValueMin = { param($C, $Rows)
  $f = $(if ($C.K -eq 'with' -or $C.K -eq 'bold' -or $C.K -eq 'chip') { $ui.F.SmallB } else { $ui.F.Small }); $w = 0
  foreach ($r in @($Rows)) { $t = & $wn.CellText $C $r; if ($t) { $w = [math]::Max($w, (& $wn.TextW $t $f)) } }
  if ($w -le 0) { return 0 }
  # a chip: its text, its own padding, the cell padding left and, right of it, at least a scroll bar's width
  if ($C.K -eq 'chip') { return ($w + (& $ui.Sc 20) + (& $ui.Sc 10) + [math]::Max((& $ui.Sc 10), [int](& $wn.BarW)) + 1) }
  return ($w + 2 * (& $ui.Sc 10) + 1) }
$wn.GridEdges = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R11 (R38): where the content of a grid's cells ends, against the room before its vertical scroll bar.
  .DESCRIPTION
  For each visible column, from the left: a chip column ends at its cell's left, the cell padding and its widest chip; the
  last visible column of another kind at its left, the padding and the widest value (never past the cell less its
  padding); the other columns end inside the grid and are not measured. Edge is the largest of these. Bar is the width of a vertical scroll bar, always reserved (the bar shows or not).
  .PARAMETER G
  The grid ($wn.Grid).
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Grid; Width (the client width); Bar; Edge; Col (the column that reaches it); Fits (R11: the grid has no chip column, or
  $wn.GridCols kept its chip whole (Tag.ChipKept); when it did not, the heads come first and the edge is not judged) }.
  #>
  param($G)
  $pd = & $ui.Sc 10; $left = 0; $edge = 0; $name = ''; $cols = @($G.Tag.Cols)
  $shown = @($G.Columns | Sort-Object DisplayIndex | Where-Object { $_.Visible }); $lastName = $(if ($shown.Count) { [string]$shown[-1].Name } else { '' })
  foreach ($k in $shown) {
    $c = @($cols | Where-Object { [string]$_.N -eq $k.Name }) | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($c.K -ne 'chip' -and [string]$k.Name -ne $lastName) { $left += $k.Width; continue }
    $f = $(if ($c.K -eq 'with' -or $c.K -eq 'bold' -or $c.K -eq 'chip') { $ui.F.SmallB } else { $ui.F.Small }); $w = 0
    foreach ($r in @($G.Tag.Shown)) { $w = [math]::Max($w, (& $wn.TextW (& $wn.CellText $c $r) $f)) }
    if ($c.K -eq 'chip') { if ($w -gt 0) { $w += & $ui.Sc 20 } }
    elseif ($c.K -eq 'pub') { $w = 0 }   # the pub column is checked by its own cut test (W1)
    $e = $left + $pd + $(if ($c.K -eq 'chip') { $w } else { [math]::Min($w, [math]::Max(0, $k.Width - 2 * $pd)) })
    if ($w -gt 0 -and $e -gt $edge) { $edge = $e; $name = [string]$k.Name }
    $left += $k.Width }
  $bar = [int](& $wn.BarW); $wd = [int]$G.ClientSize.Width
  return @{ Grid = [string]$G.AccessibleName; Width = $wd; Bar = $bar; Edge = [int]$edge; Col = $name; Fits = ($null -eq $G.Tag.ChipKept -or [bool]$G.Tag.ChipKept) } }
# R11 (R38): the LAYOUT line of grid $G when a chip or text ends closer than the scroll bar's width to the grid's right
# edge (none when it does not).
$wn.EdgeCheck = { param($G, [string]$Card)
  $e = & $wn.GridEdges $G
  if (-not $e.Fits) {   # too narrow for every head and the whole chip: the heads come first (Test-EdgeBar prints INFO); R15: but
    $sb = [int](& $wn.BarShown $G); $s = 0; foreach ($k in @($G.Columns)) { if ($k.Visible) { $s += [int]$k.Width } }   # never under a bar that shows
    if ($sb -gt 0 -and $s -gt $e.Width - $sb) { return ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' R15 grid ' + $e.Grid + ': the columns end at ' + $s + ', the grid is ' + $e.Width +
        ' wide with a scroll bar of ' + $sb + ' showing') }
    return $null }
  if ($e.Edge -gt $e.Width - $e.Bar) {
    return ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' R11 grid ' + $e.Grid + ': column ' + $e.Col + ' ends at ' + $e.Edge + ', the grid is ' + $e.Width + ' wide with a scroll bar of ' + $e.Bar) }
  return $null }
# R7 (W1): the height of one line of a pub cell, in pixels: the larger of the link font's height and its card line height.
$wn.PubLineH = { return [math]::Max([int]$ui.F.Link.Height, (& $wn.LineH $ui.F.Link)) }
# R7 (W1): the smallest width of the pub column of $Cols: its widest number, widest title ($Pw, $wn.PubWidths) or head,
# whichever is widest, plus the cell padding at both sides and 1 px; 0 when the grid has no pub column.
$wn.PubMin = { param($Cols, $Pw)
  $c = @($Cols | Where-Object { $_.K -eq 'pub' }) | Select-Object -First 1; if (-not $c) { return 0 }
  $hw = & $wn.TextW (& $wn.HeadText $c) $ui.F.SmallB
  return ([math]::Max([math]::Max([int]$Pw.Num, [int]$Pw.Title), $hw) + 2 * (& $ui.Sc 10) + 1) }
$wn.PaintPub = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Paints a pub cell: the number as a link and the title in the grid's title column, or under the number when the
  widest title of the grid does not fit in that column.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R6 (R31b D4): the title column starts after the grid's widest number and its gap (Tag.PubW, Tag.PubGap), so every
  title starts at one x; the choice beside or under is made once for the grid (Tag.PubT, the widest title), so a long
  title is never cut and the titles never start at two places. What was drawn goes into Tag.Drawn[row], relative to
  the text rectangle: the right end of the number, the title's x, the number's bottom and the title's top.
  R7 (R32 W1): also what each text needs and what it was given (number and title width, the height of the lines and
  of the cell), so the measure part and the layout self-check find a cut cell. A line is $wn.PubLineH high.
  .PARAMETER Gr
  The graphics of the cell.
  .PARAMETER Text
  The cell value, "number|title".
  .PARAMETER Tr
  The text rectangle of the cell (inside its padding).
  .PARAMETER Fl
  The one-line text flags.
  .PARAMETER Fw
  The wrapping text flags.
  .PARAMETER Tag
  The grid's Tag: PubW, PubT, PubGap and Drawn.
  .PARAMETER Row
  The row index (the key in Tag.Drawn).
  #>
  param($Gr, [string]$Text, $Tr, $Fl, $Fw, $Tag, [int]$Row)
  $pp = $Text.Split('|')
  $w1 = & $wn.TextW $pp[0] $ui.F.Link; $lh = & $wn.PubLineH
  $col = [int]$Tag.PubW + [int]$Tag.PubGap                 # the title column, from the left of the text rectangle
  $beside = ($pp.Count -lt 2 -or [int]$Tag.PubT -le $Tr.Width - $col)
  if ($beside) {
    [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[0], $ui.F.Link, $Tr, $pc.primary, $Fl)
    $tx = $col; $ty = 0; $nb = 0; $th = $lh; $tw = $Tr.Width - $col   # one line: the title's x is the column; top and bottom are not compared
    $rest = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(($Tr.X + $col), $Tr.Y, ($Tr.Width - $col), $Tr.Height)
    if ($pp.Count -gt 1) { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[1], $ui.F.Small, $rest, $pc.muted, $Fl) } }
  else {   # the widest title does not fit in the column: every title goes on a second line (the row is 2 lines high, $wn.GridHeight)
    $ny = [int](($Tr.Height - 2 * $lh) / 2); $tx = 0; $ty = $ny + $lh; $nb = $ny + $lh; $th = 2 * $lh; $tw = $Tr.Width
    [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[0], $ui.F.Link, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle($Tr.X, ($Tr.Y + $ny), $Tr.Width, $lh)), $pc.primary, $Fl)
    [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[1], $ui.F.Small, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle($Tr.X, ($Tr.Y + $ty), $Tr.Width, $lh)), $pc.muted, $Fw) }
  if ($null -eq $Tag.Drawn -or $pp.Count -lt 2) { return }
  $Tag.Drawn[$Row] = @{ NumRight = [math]::Min($w1, $Tr.Width); TitleX = $tx; NumBottom = $nb; TitleTop = $ty; Beside = $beside
    NumW = $w1; NumHave = $Tr.Width; TitleW = (& $wn.TextW $pp[1] $ui.F.Small); TitleHave = $tw; NeedH = $th; HaveH = $Tr.Height } }
# Paints a status chip cell: a rounded fill of the row's chip kind with the status in the middle. $Bd: the cell bounds; $Pd: its padding.
$wn.PaintChip = { param($Gr, [string]$Text, [string]$Kind, $Bd, [int]$Pd)
  $cwid = [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText($Text, $ui.F.SmallB, ([Drawing.Size]::new(100000, 0)), [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'NoPadding, NoPrefix').Width + (& $ui.Sc 20)
  $chh = & $ui.Sc 26; $cy = $Bd.Y + [int](($Bd.Height - 1 - $chh) / 2); $rc = New-Object System.Drawing.RectangleF(($Bd.X + $Pd), $cy, $cwid, $chh)
  $Gr.SmoothingMode = 'AntiAlias'; $path = [Pfm.Gfx]::Round($rc, ($chh / 2.0)); $br = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush($wn.Fills[$Kind]); $Gr.FillPath($br, $path); $br.Dispose(); $path.Dispose()
  $Gr.SmoothingMode = 'Default'
  $tf = [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'HorizontalCenter, VerticalCenter, SingleLine, NoPadding, NoPrefix'
  [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $Text, $ui.F.SmallB, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(($Bd.X + $Pd), $cy, [int]$cwid, $chh)), $pc.ink, $tf) }
$wn.PaintCell = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Paints one grid cell (the CellPainting event): the header in muted capitals with a line under it, or a row cell by its column kind.
  .PARAMETER S
  The grid.
  .PARAMETER E
  The event arguments (cell bounds, graphics, value; Handled is set).
  #>
  param($S, $E)
  try {
    $tag = $S.Tag; $kind = [string]$tag.Kind[$S.Columns[$E.ColumnIndex].Name]; $bd = $E.CellBounds; $gr = $E.Graphics; $pd = & $ui.Sc 10
    $fl = [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'Left, VerticalCenter, SingleLine, NoPadding, NoPrefix, EndEllipsis'
    $fw = [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'Left, VerticalCenter, WordBreak, NoPadding, NoPrefix'
    $tr = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(($bd.X + $pd), $bd.Y, [math]::Max(1, $bd.Width - 2 * $pd), ($bd.Height - 1))
    $head = ($E.RowIndex -lt 0)
    $bg = $(if (-not $head -and $S.Rows[$E.RowIndex].Selected) { $pc.surface } else { $ui.C.White })
    $br = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush($bg); $gr.FillRectangle($br, $bd); $br.Dispose()
    $pn = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen($(if ($head) { $pc.muted } else { $pc.line }), 1); $gr.DrawLine($pn, $bd.X, ($bd.Bottom - 1), $bd.Right, ($bd.Bottom - 1)); $pn.Dispose()
    $text = [string]$E.Value
    if ($head) {
      $cd = @(@($tag.Cols) | Where-Object { [string]$_.N -eq [string]$S.Columns[$E.ColumnIndex].Name }) | Select-Object -First 1
      $wrapHead = [bool]($cd -and $cd.HW)   # R11: a head that wraps to 2 lines (WordBreak) and needs the width of its wider line
      [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text.ToUpperInvariant(), $ui.F.SmallB, $tr, $pc.muted, $(if ($wrapHead) { $fw } else { $fl }))
      # R7 (W1): what the head of the pub column needs and has, for the measure part and the layout self-check
      $hd = @{ Text = $text.ToUpperInvariant(); W = $(if ($wrapHead) { (& $wn.HeadWrap $cd) } else { (& $wn.TextW $text.ToUpperInvariant() $ui.F.SmallB) }); Have = $tr.Width; Kind = $kind }
      if ($kind -eq 'pub') { $tag.Head = $hd }
      if ($null -ne $tag.Heads) { $tag.Heads[[string]$S.Columns[$E.ColumnIndex].Name] = $hd } }   # R8 (W7): every head, for the same checks
    elseif ($kind -eq 'pub') { & $wn.PaintPub $gr $text $tr $fl $fw $tag $E.RowIndex }
    elseif ($kind -eq 'with') { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text, $ui.F.SmallB, $tr, $pc.navy, $fw) }
    elseif ($kind -eq 'bold') { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text, $ui.F.SmallB, $tr, $pc.ink, $fw) }
    elseif ($kind -eq 'chip') { & $wn.PaintChip $gr $text ([string]$tag.Chip[$text]) $bd $pd }
    else { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text, $ui.F.Small, $tr, $ui.C.Ink, $fw) }
    $E.Handled = $true
  } catch { $null = $_ } }
# Opens the card of grid row $I after the current event has ended (a card change inside a grid event would dispose the grid in its own handler).
$wn.Later = { param($G, [int]$I) $wn.PendG = $G; $wn.PendI = $I; [void]$form.BeginInvoke([Action]{ & $wn.OpenRow $wn.PendG $wn.PendI }) }
# Opens the card that grid row $I goes to, as its Open button would.
$wn.OpenRow = { param($G, [int]$I)
  $r = @($G.Tag.Shown)[$I]
  if ($r -and $r.Go) { & $wn.Press @{ Go = [string]$r.Go; Text = 'Open' } } }
# Filters the All Actions grid by the search text and the "Show" choice, and updates its count line.
$wn.Refilter = {
  $g = $wn.Gridq; if (-not $g) { return }
  $q = ([string]$wn.Field.find).Trim(); $m = [int]$wn.Field.show
  $rows = @($GridQueue | Where-Object { ($m -eq 0 -or ($m -eq 1 -and $_.Me) -or ($m -eq 2 -and $_.Kind -eq 'late')) -and
      (-not $q -or ([string]$_.Publication).IndexOf($q, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) -ge 0) })
  & $wn.GridFill $g $rows; $g.ClearSelection()
  if ($wn.CountBox) { $wn.CountBox.Text = ([string]$wn.CountText -f $rows.Count) } }
'@ }
