<#
.SYNOPSIS
  90-161.Z Task 22 r15, part "measure": the script's own accessible-name check (the RESULT NAMES line) and the -Measure
  run, which builds every card off-screen and writes what it measured as JSON for tests/ps/Test-T22Layout.ps1.
.DESCRIPTION
  R13 (R40): the measure file has Keep (each card opened again from its kept page, $wn.MeasureKeep in the keep part).
  R11 (R38; PFM 20 Nov 26): the measure file has Edges (the right edge of each grid) and one Fulcrum logo (Theme.Fulcrum, ShownDiff).
  Names (R30 fallback for check 8, Narrator names): every button, link, check box, choice, text box and list of every
  card, the rail and the check bar must have an accessible name; the result is one line "RESULT NAMES PASS" or
  "RESULT NAMES FAIL (<n> controls: <card>/<type> "<text>", ...)".
  Measure (-Measure <file>): the window is built at 1280 x 720 far off the screen and never shown to a person; for each
  card it records the crumb (fonts, bounds, the ink gap after the link: R30 V2), every button (its color and the color
  of its face as drawn: V4) and every section card (its bottom: V4). R31: it also records the rail head at this scale
  and at 1.5 x (W1: the logo's middle and the name's middle, the color behind the logo) and the colors that
  Select-T22Color gives with high contrast on and off (W2). No question; no file but the given one and the card
  pictures next to it.
  Level (R6, R31b D1 to D4): $wn.LevelFacts gives, for the card on the page, the middles of each Action Status caption
  and the main card's first line (D1), of the crumb's link and rest with their font sizes (D2), of each check chip and
  its first text line (D3), and where each pub grid drew its numbers and titles (D4). -Measure records them for every
  card at this scale and again at 1.25 x and 1.5 x ($wn.MeasureScaled); the layout self-check turns them into LAYOUT lines
  ($ui.Measure, $wn.LevelBad), so the window flags the 4 defects on the device too.
  R7 (R32 W1 to W3): the level facts also hold every chip beside text with its kind (W3) and, for each pub grid, what
  its head and each cell needed and had (W1); the self-check writes a W1 or W3 LAYOUT line for each one out of line.
  $wn.MeasureWheel turns the mouse wheel through the window's own filter with no real pointer (W2).
  R8 (R35 W7): $wn.LogoFacts and $wn.LogoBad check the rail logo's colors each time the rail is built (the window
  part calls them); $wn.MeasureLogo rebuilds the window with high contrast on and off and records the logo facts.
  Card pictures (R31 W4): $wn.SavePng saves the window as it shows a card, 90161Z-T22-card-<card>-r15.png, in
  $wn.PngDir (the T22 folder in a normal run, the folder of the measure file with -Measure); $wn.PngLines adds the
  CARDPNG lines to the result. The cards hold FAKE data or (R14) fake rows of the test site; a card with a site row that
  has no fake-data marker gets no picture. A picture that cannot be saved is a NOTE line.
  Inputs: $form, $page, $rail, $pc, $ui, $wn, $Cards, $Rev, $lines. Outputs: $wn.NoName, $wn.NamesLine, $wn.SavePng,
  $wn.PngLines, $wn.LevelFacts, $wn.LevelBad, $wn.PubCut, $ui.Measure, $wn.MeasureWheel, $wn.LogoFacts, $wn.LogoBad,
  $wn.MeasureLogo, $wn.MeasureRun and its helpers.
  Run: not alone; 90161Z-T22-pfm-window-r15.ps1 dot-sources it from its own folder inside its try block.
  Network: none.
  Writes: the card PNG files in $wn.PngDir (the T22 folder, or -TestDir); with -Measure: the JSON file given and the
  card PNG files in its folder (the test gives a file in its own temporary folder).
  Credentials: none.
#>
$wn.NoName = [ordered]@{}; $wn.Scanned = $false
$wn.PngDir = ''; $wn.Pngs = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$wn.SavePng = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Saves a picture of the window as it shows card $Key (R31 W4): 90161Z-T22-card-<key>-r15.png in $wn.PngDir.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Control.DrawToBitmap at the window's current size; nothing when $wn.PngDir is empty. A picture that cannot be
  saved is a NOTE line in the result, not a stop. The file name is kept in $wn.Pngs.
  R14 (R41): no picture of a card that shows a site row without a fake-data marker (Get-SiteUnmarked, site part); a
  CARDPNG line says so.
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key (the card on the page).
  #>
  param([string]$Key)
  if (-not $wn.PngDir) { return }
  $name = '90161Z-T22-card-' + $Key + '-' + $Rev + '.png'
  # R14 (R41; PFM 20 Nov 26): a card that shows a site row with no fake-data marker gets no picture (the site part)
  $bad = Get-SiteUnmarked $Key
  if ($bad -gt 0) { $lines.Add('CARDPNG ' + $Key + ' not saved: ' + $bad + ' site rows without a fake-data marker'); return }
  try {
    $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $form.Width), [math]::Max(1, $form.Height))
    try {
      $form.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height)))
      $bm.Save((Join-Path $wn.PngDir $name), [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png); $wn.Pngs.Add($name)
    } finally { $bm.Dispose() }
  } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE card picture not saved: ' + $name + ' (' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message) + ')') } }
# The CARDPNG lines of the result: how many card pictures were saved of how many cards, then one line per file name.
$wn.PngLines = {
  if (-not $wn.PngDir) { return }
  $lines.Add('CARDPNG saved=' + $wn.Pngs.Count + ' of ' + $Cards.Count)
  foreach ($n in $wn.Pngs) { $lines.Add('CARDPNG ' + $n) } }
$wn.NameScan = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Notes each button, link, check box, choice, text box and list under $Root that has no accessible name.
  .PARAMETER Card
  The card key (or rail, bar) the controls belong to; it starts each note.
  .PARAMETER Root
  The control whose children are read (the page, the rail or the check bar).
  #>
  param([string]$Card, $Root)
  if (-not $Root) { return }
  $wn.Scanned = $true; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($Root)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      $named = ($c -is [Windows.Forms.ButtonBase] -or $c -is [Windows.Forms.TextBoxBase] -or $c -is [Windows.Forms.ComboBox])
      if ($named -and -not ([string]$c.AccessibleName).Trim()) {
        $t = ([string]$c.Text).Trim(); if ($t.Length -gt 24) { $t = $t.Substring(0, 24) + '...' }
        $wn.NoName[$Card + '/' + $c.GetType().Name + ' "' + $t + '"'] = 1 }
      if ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } } }
# The RESULT NAMES line: PASS, or FAIL with the number of controls without a name and which ones.
$wn.NamesLine = {
  if ($wn.NoName.Count -eq 0) { return 'RESULT NAMES PASS' }
  return ('RESULT NAMES FAIL (' + $wn.NoName.Count + ' controls: ' + (@($wn.NoName.Keys) -join ', ') + ')') }
$wn.InkSpan = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Where the ink of a control starts and ends, left to right, as drawn.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Draws the control into a bitmap and finds the first and the last pixel column that differs from its background by
  more than 90 (the RADE ink rule, $ui.Ink: the sum of the red, green and blue distances).
  .PARAMETER C
  The control.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ First; Last } in the control's own pixels; -1 when nothing was drawn.
  #>
  param($C)
  $out = @{ First = -1; Last = -1 }
  try {
    $w = [math]::Max(1, $C.Width); $h = [math]::Max(1, $C.Height); $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap($w, $h)
    try {
      $C.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $w, $h))); $bg = $C.BackColor
      for ($x = 0; $x -lt $w; $x++) {
        for ($y = 0; $y -lt $h; $y++) {
          $p = $bm.GetPixel($x, $y)
          if ([math]::Abs($p.R - $bg.R) + [math]::Abs($p.G - $bg.G) + [math]::Abs($p.B - $bg.B) -gt 90) { if ($out.First -lt 0) { $out.First = $x }; $out.Last = $x; break } } }
    } finally { $bm.Dispose() }
  } catch { $null = $_ }
  return $out }
# A color as #RRGGBB.
$wn.Hex = { param($Color) return ('#{0:X2}{1:X2}{2:X2}' -f $Color.R, $Color.G, $Color.B) }
# The color of a button's face as drawn: the pixel 6 px right of and 4 px under its top left corner (inside its edge, above its text).
$wn.FaceColor = { param($B)
  try {
    $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $B.Width), [math]::Max(1, $B.Height))
    try { $B.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height))); return (& $wn.Hex $bm.GetPixel((& $wn.Sc 6), (& $wn.Sc 4))) } finally { $bm.Dispose() }
  } catch { return '' } }
# A font as a table: name, size in points, style and height in pixels.
$wn.FontFacts = { param($F) return [ordered]@{ Name = $F.Name; Size = [double]$F.SizeInPoints; Style = [string]$F.Style; Height = [int]$F.Height } }
$wn.MeasureCrumb = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The crumb of the card on the page: its link and rest, their fonts and bounds, and the gap after the link.
  .DESCRIPTION
  GapInk: the empty pixel columns between the last ink of the link (its underline ends with its text) and the first ink
  of the rest (the arrow), as drawn. GapBounds: the distance between the two controls.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table, or $null when the card has no crumb link.
  #>
  $l = $wn.CrumbLink; $t = $wn.CrumbRest; if (-not $l -or -not $t) { return $null }
  $li = & $wn.InkSpan $l; $ti = & $wn.InkSpan $t
  $gap = $(if ($li.Last -ge 0 -and $ti.First -ge 0) { ($t.Left + $ti.First) - ($l.Left + $li.Last) - 1 } else { $null })
  return [ordered]@{ Link = [string]$l.Text; Rest = [string]$t.Text; LinkFont = (& $wn.FontFacts $l.Font); RestFont = (& $wn.FontFacts $t.Font)
    LinkBounds = [string]$l.Bounds; RestBounds = [string]$t.Bounds; LinkInk = $li.Last; RestInk = $ti.First; GapBounds = ($t.Left - $l.Right); GapInk = $gap } }
$wn.LevelPubs = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R6 (R31b D4): where each grid with a pub column on the page drew its numbers and titles.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Each such grid is drawn once into a bitmap (so its cells are painted now, also off-screen); $wn.PaintPub keeps what
  it drew in the grid's Tag.Drawn, relative to the cell's text rectangle. Rows that are scrolled out of the grid are
  not drawn and not listed.
  R7 (R32 W1): also the head of the pub column (its text, the width it needs and has) and, per row drawn, the widths
  and heights the number and title needed and had ($wn.PaintPub).
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per grid: Grid (its name), Gap (the gap after the widest number), Rows (rows drawn), Head, HeadW, HeadHave
  and, one value per row drawn, Beside, TitleX, NumRight, NumBottom, TitleTop, NumW, NumHave, TitleW, TitleHave, NeedH
  and HaveH.
  #>
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) {
        if (-not ($c.Tag -is [hashtable]) -or -not (@($c.Tag.Kind.Values) -contains 'pub')) { continue }
        $c.Tag.Drawn = @{}; $c.Tag.Head = $null
        try { $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $c.Width), [math]::Max(1, $c.Height))
          try { $c.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height))) } finally { $bm.Dispose() } } catch { $null = $_ }
        $d = @(foreach ($k in @($c.Tag.Drawn.Keys | Sort-Object)) { $c.Tag.Drawn[$k] })
        $g = [ordered]@{}; $g['Grid'] = [string]$c.AccessibleName; $g['Gap'] = [int]$c.Tag.PubGap; $g['Rows'] = $d.Count
        $h = $c.Tag.Head; $g['Head'] = $(if ($h) { [string]$h.Text } else { '' }); $g['HeadW'] = $(if ($h) { [int]$h.W } else { 0 }); $g['HeadHave'] = $(if ($h) { [int]$h.Have } else { 0 })
        foreach ($n in 'Beside', 'TitleX', 'NumRight', 'NumBottom', 'TitleTop', 'NumW', 'NumHave', 'TitleW', 'TitleHave', 'NeedH', 'HaveH') { $g[$n] = @($d | ForEach-Object { $_[$n] }) }
        $out.Add($g) }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.LevelHeads = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R8 (R35 W7, R34 open point 5): the column heads of every grid on the page, as the grid drew them.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Each grid is drawn once into a bitmap (so its head is painted now, also off-screen); $wn.PaintCell keeps each head
  it drew in the grid's Tag.Heads: its text in capitals, the width it needs and the width its cell gave it.
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per head: Grid (its name), Col (the column name), Kind, Head (the text), W (needed) and Have.
  #>
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) {
        if (-not ($c.Tag -is [hashtable])) { continue }
        $c.Tag.Heads = [ordered]@{}
        try { $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $c.Width), [math]::Max(1, $c.Height))
          try { $c.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height))) } finally { $bm.Dispose() } } catch { $null = $_ }
        foreach ($k in @($c.Tag.Heads.Keys)) { $h = $c.Tag.Heads[$k]
          $r = [ordered]@{}; $r['Grid'] = [string]$c.AccessibleName; $r['Col'] = [string]$k; $r['Kind'] = [string]$h.Kind; $r['Head'] = [string]$h.Text
          $r['W'] = [int]$h.W; $r['Have'] = [int]$h.Have; $out.Add($r) } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.LevelEdges = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R11 (R38): where the chips and last-column text of every grid on the page end, against the grid's right edge.
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per grid ($wn.GridEdges): Grid, Width, Bar, Edge, Col, Fits.
  #>
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) { if ($c.Tag -is [hashtable]) { $out.Add((& $wn.GridEdges $c)) } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.LevelFacts = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R6 (R31b D1 to D4): the alignment facts of the card on the page, in page pixels ($wn.TextMid).
  .DESCRIPTION
  Caps (D1): for each Action Status card, the middle of its caption and of the first line of the main card. Crumb (D2):
  the font size and text middle of the crumb's link and rest, or $null when the card has no crumb link. Chips (D3, R7
  W3): for each chip beside text ($wn.ChipRows: check, list, rows, chips, notice), its kind, the middle of the chip and
  of the first line of its text. Pubs (D4, R7 W1): $wn.LevelPubs. Heads (R8 W7): $wn.LevelHeads.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Caps, Crumb, Chips, Pubs, Heads, Edges (R11: $wn.LevelEdges).
  #>
  $mainSec = @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Col -eq 0 }) | Select-Object -First 1
  $line = $(if ($mainSec) { & $wn.FirstLine $mainSec.Card } else { $null })
  $caps = @(foreach ($s in @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Stretch -and $_.CapBox -and $line })) {
      $c = [ordered]@{}; $c['Cap'] = [string]$s.CapBox.Text; $c['CapMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $s.CapBox); $c['Line'] = [string]$line.Text; $c['LineMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $line); $c })
  $crumb = $null; $l = $wn.CrumbLink; $t = $wn.CrumbRest
  if ($l -and $t) { $crumb = [ordered]@{}; $crumb['LinkSize'] = [double]$l.Font.SizeInPoints; $crumb['RestSize'] = [double]$t.Font.SizeInPoints
    $crumb['LinkMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $l); $crumb['RestMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $t) }
  $chips = @(foreach ($r in @($wn.ChipRows)) {
      $c = [ordered]@{}; $c['Chip'] = [string]$r.Chip.Text; $c['Kind'] = [string]$r.Kind; $c['ChipMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $r.Chip)
      $c['Line'] = [string]$r.Text.Text; $c['LineMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $r.Text); $c })
  $f = [ordered]@{}; $f['Caps'] = $caps; $f['Crumb'] = $crumb; $f['Chips'] = $chips; $f['Pubs'] = @(& $wn.LevelPubs); $f['Heads'] = @(& $wn.LevelHeads); $f['Edges'] = @(& $wn.LevelEdges)
  return $f }
# R7 (W1): the cut cells of one measured pub grid $P ($wn.LevelPubs), one short text per row: "row <n> number 120>96"
# when its number, title or lines needed more pixels than the cell gave; none when every cell holds its text.
$wn.PubCut = { param($P)
  $out = @(); $nw = @($P.NumW); $nh = @($P.NumHave); $tw = @($P.TitleW); $th = @($P.TitleHave); $lh = @($P.NeedH); $ch = @($P.HaveH)
  for ($i = 0; $i -lt [int]$P.Rows; $i++) {
    $bad = @(); if ([int]$nw[$i] -gt [int]$nh[$i]) { $bad += ('number ' + $nw[$i] + '>' + $nh[$i]) }
    if ([int]$tw[$i] -gt [int]$th[$i]) { $bad += ('title ' + $tw[$i] + '>' + $th[$i]) }
    if ([int]$lh[$i] -gt [int]$ch[$i]) { $bad += ('height ' + $lh[$i] + '>' + $ch[$i]) }
    if ($bad.Count) { $out += ('row ' + ($i + 1) + ' ' + ($bad -join ', ')) } }
  return $out }
$wn.LevelBad = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The LAYOUT lines of the layout self-check for D1 to D4 (R6): each fact of $wn.LevelFacts that is out of line.
  .DESCRIPTION
  D1, D2 and D3: two middles more than $Tol apart (D2 also: two font sizes). D4: the titles of a grid start at more than
  one x, or a title in the column starts before the end of the widest number and the gap, or a title under its number
  starts above the number's bottom. A grid with no row drawn has nothing to compare.
  R7 (R32): W1: the head of a pub column needs more width than it has (it would be shortened with dots), or a pub cell
  is cut (its number or title needs more width, or its lines more height, than the cell gave). W3: the D3 rule for
  every chip beside text; the line names the chip's kind.
  R8 (R35 W7): a column head other than the pub head (W1 has that one) needs more width than it has: one line per grid
  that names each cut head.
  .PARAMETER Card
  The card key (it starts each line).
  .PARAMETER F
  The facts ($wn.LevelFacts).
  .PARAMETER Tol
  The tolerance in pixels: 1 px at 100 %, scaled.
  .OUTPUTS
  The LAYOUT lines (none when all is in line).
  #>
  param([string]$Card, $F, [double]$Tol)
  $out = @()
  foreach ($c in @($F.Caps)) { if ([math]::Abs($c.CapMid - $c.LineMid) -gt $Tol) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D1 caption "' + $c.Cap + '" middle ' + $c.CapMid + ', the first line of the main card ' + $c.LineMid) } }
  $k = $F.Crumb
  if ($k -and ($k.LinkSize -ne $k.RestSize -or [math]::Abs($k.LinkMid - $k.RestMid) -gt $Tol)) {
    $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D2 crumb: link ' + $k.LinkSize + ' pt middle ' + $k.LinkMid + ', rest ' + $k.RestSize + ' pt middle ' + $k.RestMid) }
  foreach ($c in @($F.Chips)) { if ([math]::Abs($c.ChipMid - $c.LineMid) -gt $Tol) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W3 chip "' + $c.Chip + '" (' + $c.Kind + ') middle ' + $c.ChipMid + ', its first text line ' + $c.LineMid) } }
  foreach ($p in @($F.Pubs)) {
    if ($p.Head -and [int]$p.HeadW -gt [int]$p.HeadHave) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W1 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': the head "' + $p.Head + '" needs ' + $p.HeadW + ' px, has ' + $p.HeadHave) }
    $cut = @(& $wn.PubCut $p)
    if ($cut.Count) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W1 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': ' + $cut.Count + ' publication cells cut (' + ($cut -join '; ') + ')') }
    if ([int]$p.Rows -lt 1) { continue }
    $xs = @($p.TitleX | Sort-Object -Unique); $num = [int](@($p.NumRight) | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum
    $under = @(for ($i = 0; $i -lt [int]$p.Rows; $i++) { if (-not $p.Beside[$i] -and $p.TitleTop[$i] -lt $p.NumBottom[$i]) { $i } })
    if ($xs.Count -gt 1) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D4 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': the titles start at ' + ($xs -join ', ')) }
    elseif ((@($p.Beside) -contains $true) -and [int]$xs[0] -lt $num + [int]$p.Gap) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D4 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': the titles start at ' + $xs[0] + ', the widest number ends at ' + $num) }
    elseif ($under.Count) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D4 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': ' + $under.Count + ' titles start above the bottom of their number') } }
  $cut = @($F.Heads | Where-Object { $_ -and [string]$_.Kind -ne 'pub' -and [int]$_.W -gt [int]$_.Have })
  foreach ($g in @($cut | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.Grid } | Sort-Object -Unique)) {
    $list = @($cut | Where-Object { [string]$_.Grid -eq $g } | ForEach-Object { '"' + $_.Head + '" needs ' + $_.W + ' px, has ' + $_.Have })
    $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W7 grid ' + $g + ': ' + $list.Count + ' column heads cut (' + ($list -join '; ') + ')') }
  return $out }
# The self-check's extra lines (the rade-ui block calls $ui.Measure for each card it checks): D1 to D4, 1 px at 100 %.
$ui.Measure = { param($Card) return @(& $wn.LevelBad $Card (& $wn.LevelFacts) ([math]::Max(1.0, $ui.Dpi / 96.0))) }
$wn.MeasureCard = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  What -Measure records for the card on the page: the crumb, every button and link, every section card, and the
  alignment facts of D1 to D4 (R6).
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Key, Crumb, Buttons (Text, Link, Back, Face, Edge), Sections (Col, Cap, Stretch, Top, Bottom; page pixels),
  Level ($wn.LevelFacts).
  #>
  param([string]$Key)
  $btns = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.Button]) {
        $b = [ordered]@{}; $b['Text'] = [string]$c.Text; $b['Link'] = ([int]$c.FlatAppearance.BorderSize -eq 0)
        $b['Back'] = (& $wn.Hex $c.BackColor); $b['Face'] = (& $wn.FaceColor $c); $b['Edge'] = (& $wn.Hex $c.FlatAppearance.BorderColor)
        $btns.Add($b) }
      if ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  $pt = $page.RectangleToScreen($page.ClientRectangle).Top
  $secs = @(foreach ($s in $wn.Secs) { $r = $s.Card.RectangleToScreen($s.Card.ClientRectangle)
      [ordered]@{ Col = $s.Col; Cap = $s.Cap; Stretch = $s.Stretch; Top = ($r.Top - $pt); Bottom = ($r.Bottom - $pt) } })
  # One key per statement: Windows PowerShell 5.1 stops on an [ordered] literal that holds a generic list (R30 CI).
  $card = [ordered]@{}; $card['Key'] = $Key; $card['Crumb'] = (& $wn.MeasureCrumb)
  $card['Buttons'] = $btns.ToArray(); $card['Sections'] = $secs; $card['Level'] = (& $wn.LevelFacts)
  return $card }
$wn.MeasureScaled = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Builds every card again at $K times this scale and gives back the alignment facts of D1 to D4 of each (R6).
  .DESCRIPTION
  As $wn.MeasureHead does for the rail head: the scale ($ui.Dpi), the font factor and every font of $ui.F (with the
  crumb font and the step fonts made from them) are $K times as large, as Windows makes them at that scale. Each card is
  shown and measured ($wn.LevelFacts); a card that cannot be measured keeps its error. Then the scale and the fonts come
  back, Your Work is shown again and the scaled fonts are disposed.
  .PARAMETER K
  The factor (1.5: the PFM's 150 %).
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: K, Dpi, Sc8 (8 px at 100 %, at this scale), Cards (Key, Level or Error) and (R7 W2) Wheel ($wn.MeasureWheel)
  or WheelError.
  #>
  param([double]$K)
  $keep = @{ Dpi = $ui.Dpi; FontK = $ui.FontK; F = $ui.F; Crumb = $wn.CrumbFont; Step = $wn.StepFonts }
  $made = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $cards = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $res = [ordered]@{}
  try {
    $nf = @{}; foreach ($n in @($keep.F.Keys)) { $o = $keep.F[$n]; $x = New-Object System.Drawing.Font($o.FontFamily, [single]($o.Size * $K), $o.Style); $nf[$n] = $x; $made.Add($x) }
    $ui.Dpi = $keep.Dpi * $K; $ui.FontK = $keep.FontK * $K; $ui.F = $nf; $wn.StepFonts = $null
    $wn.CrumbFont = New-Object System.Drawing.Font($nf.Small, [Enum]::Parse(('System.Drawing.FontStyle' -as [type]), 'Underline')); $made.Add($wn.CrumbFont)
    $res['K'] = $K; $res['Dpi'] = $ui.Dpi; $res['Sc8'] = (& $wn.Sc 8)
    foreach ($key in $Cards.Keys) {
      $c = [ordered]@{}; $c['Key'] = $key
      try { $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show $key; [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents(); $c['Level'] = (& $wn.LevelFacts); $c['Btn'] = @(& $wn.BtnLines) }
      catch { $c['Error'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
      $cards.Add($c) }
    # R7 (W2): the mouse wheel at this scale too; a wheel case that cannot run is kept as its error (the test names it).
    try { $res['Wheel'] = (& $wn.MeasureWheel) } catch { $res['Wheel'] = $null; $res['WheelError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  } finally {
    if ($wn.StepFonts -and -not [object]::ReferenceEquals($wn.StepFonts, $keep.Step)) { foreach ($x in @($wn.StepFonts.A) + @($wn.StepFonts.B)) { $made.Add($x) } }
    $ui.Dpi = $keep.Dpi; $ui.FontK = $keep.FontK; $ui.F = $keep.F; $wn.CrumbFont = $keep.Crumb; $wn.StepFonts = $keep.Step
    & $wn.KeepClear; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home'   # R13: no kept card keeps the scaled fonts disposed below
    foreach ($x in $made) { try { $x.Dispose() } catch { $null = $_ } } }
  $res['Cards'] = $cards.ToArray()
  return $res }
# R11 (R38; UI standard v1, B1): the B1 lines ($ui.BtnBad) of every shown RADE button of the page, at the scale in use
# (the self-check runs at the window's own scale only; this one runs at 1.25 x and 1.5 x too). None when all are right.
$wn.BtnLines = {
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.Button] -and $c.Visible -and $ui.BtnKind.ContainsKey($c)) { foreach ($l in @(& $ui.BtnBad 'scaled' ([string]$c.AccessibleName) $c)) { $out.Add([string]$l) } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.LogoFacts = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R8 (R35 W7): what the rail logo shows now, for the self-check and the measure part.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: High (the colors in use: $ui.High), Shown (a logo is on the rail), Other (its pixels with any cover that are
  neither of the 2 system colors of $wn.LogoRole) and Diff (its pixels that differ from the logo in its own colors);
  -1 when no logo is shown.
  #>
  $f = [ordered]@{}; $f['High'] = [bool]$ui.High; $f['Shown'] = $false; $f['Other'] = -1; $f['Diff'] = -1
  $lg = $wn.Logo; if (-not $lg -or -not $lg.Image) { return $f }
  $own = & $wn.LogoImage $false; $d = [string]$wn.LogoRole.Dark; $l = [string]$wn.LogoRole.Light
  try { $f['Shown'] = $true; $f['Other'] = [Pfm.Logo]::Other($lg.Image, [Drawing.SystemColors]::$d, [Drawing.SystemColors]::$l); $f['Diff'] = [Pfm.Logo]::Diff($lg.Image, $own) }
  finally { $own.Dispose() }
  return $f }
# R8 (R35 W7): the LAYOUT line for logo facts $F ($wn.LogoFacts) with the wrong colors, or none: with high contrast on,
# a pixel in another color or no change from the own colors; with it off, any pixel that differs from the own colors.
$wn.LogoBad = { param($F)
  if (-not $F.Shown) { return @() }
  if ($F.High -and ([int]$F.Other -ne 0 -or [int]$F.Diff -eq 0)) {
    return @('LAYOUT rail W7 logo: high contrast on, ' + $F.Other + ' pixels not in the system colors, ' + $F.Diff + ' pixels changed from its own colors') }
  if (-not $F.High -and [int]$F.Diff -ne 0) { return @('LAYOUT rail W7 logo: high contrast off, ' + $F.Diff + ' pixels differ from its own colors') }
  return @() }
$wn.HeadFacts = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The facts of one rail head (R31 W1): the bounds of the logo and the name, their vertical middles and the colors
  behind the logo and behind the panel it sits on.
  .PARAMETER Logo
  The logo picture box.

  .PARAMETER At

  param($Logo, $Name, $Into, [string]$At)
  $f = [ordered]@{}; $f['At'] = $At; $f['Logo'] = [string]$Logo.Bounds; $f['Name'] = [string]$Name.Bounds
  $f['LogoMid'] = $Logo.Top + $Logo.Height / 2.0; $f['NameMid'] = $Name.Top + $Name.Height / 2.0
  $f['LogoBack'] = (& $wn.Hex $Logo.BackColor); $f['RailBack'] = (& $wn.Hex $Into.BackColor)
  return $f }
$wn.MeasureHead = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The rail head at this screen's scale (the rail as built) and at 1.5 x that scale (R31 W1).
  .DESCRIPTION
  For 1.5 x, the same builder ($wn.HeadParts) runs into a navy test panel on the window with the scale ($ui.Dpi) and

$wn.MeasureContrast = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The colors Select-T22Color gives for each palette name with high contrast on and off (R31 W2), with no change of the
  Windows theme.
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per palette name and setting: Table (pc or C), Key, High, System (a system color), Name (its color name),
  Role (the system color its role names), Hex and Own (the window's own color).
  #>
  $rows = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
  foreach ($t in @(@{ Name = 'pc'; Own = $ui.OwnPc }, @{ Name = 'C'; Own = $ui.OwnC })) {
    foreach ($high in $true, $false) {
      $pick = Select-T22Color $high $t.Own $ui.HcRole
      foreach ($k in @($pick.Keys | Sort-Object)) {
        $r = [ordered]@{}; $r['Table'] = $t.Name; $r['Key'] = [string]$k; $r['High'] = $high; $r['System'] = [bool]$pick[$k].IsSystemColor
        $r['Name'] = [string]$pick[$k].Name; $r['Role'] = [string]$ui.HcRole[$k]; $r['Hex'] = (& $wn.Hex $pick[$k]); $r['Own'] = (& $wn.Hex $t.Own[$k])
        $rows.Add($r) } } }
  return $rows.ToArray() }
$wn.MeasureLogo = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R8 (R35 W7): the rail logo with high contrast on, then off, with no change of the Windows theme.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The window is recolored both ways ($wn.Recolor with -Force: the rail, the check bar and the card are rebuilt, as on a
  real change of the setting) and the logo facts are taken after each rebuild. Then the window takes the Windows
  setting again.
  .OUTPUTS
  Two tables of $wn.LogoFacts (on, then off), each with When and Bad (the LAYOUT lines of $wn.LogoBad).
  #>
  $res = @()
  try {
    foreach ($h in $true, $false) {

      $f = & $wn.LogoFacts; $f['When'] = $(if ($h) { 'on' } else { 'off' }); $f['Bad'] = @(& $wn.LogoBad $f); $res += , $f }
  } finally { if ([bool]$ui.High -ne [bool][Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::HighContrast) { & $wn.Recolor 'measure back' } }
  return $res }
$wn.WheelTry = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R7 (R32 W2): turns the mouse wheel once towards you (delta -120) at point $Pt of the window, in 2 ways: through the
  window's own filter (Pfm.Wheel.PreFilterMessage, as Windows calls it, with the message sent to the control that has
  the focus and the pointer in screen pixels), or straight through the routing function on the control tree.
  .PARAMETER Filter
  The filter ($wn.WheelNew).
  .PARAMETER Pt
  The pointer, in client pixels of the window ($wn.ViewMid).
  .PARAMETER Focus
  The control the message is for (Windows sends the wheel to the control with the focus).
  .PARAMETER Direct
  When set, the routing function Pfm.Wheel.Route is called with $Pt; no message, no screen pixels.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Handled (the turn was taken); Under (the control under the pointer: its type and accessible name) }.
  #>
  param($Filter, $Pt, $Focus, [switch]$Direct)
  $u = [Pfm.Wheel]::Under($form, $Pt)
  if ($Direct) { $ok = ($null -ne [Pfm.Wheel]::Route($form, $main, $Pt, -120)) }
  else { $m = [Pfm.Wheel]::Make($Focus.Handle, $form.PointToScreen($Pt), -120); $ok = $Filter.PreFilterMessage([ref]$m) }
  return @{ Handled = [bool]$ok; Under = ($u.GetType().Name + ' "' + [string]$u.AccessibleName + '"') } }
$wn.WheelCase = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R7 (R32 W2): one wheel case on Your Work at its top: one turn on the middle of its first card ("Needs You Today"),
  then, when a grid of the card has rows out of view, the card is scrolled to the grid and one turn goes to the middle
  of the grid's part in view ($wn.WheelTry; a button has the focus).
  .PARAMETER Direct
  When set, the turns go straight to the routing function; else through the window's filter.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Scrolls, Point (the pointer, window pixels), PageTop, Under, Handled, Before, After (the main column's
  scroll position) and, when a grid can scroll,
  GridUnder, GridHandled, GridBefore, GridAfter (its first row in view) and MainBefore, MainAfter.
  #>
  param([switch]$Direct)
  $res = [ordered]@{}; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home'
  [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents(); $main.AutoScrollPosition = [Drawing.Point]::new(0, 0)
  $flt = & $wn.WheelNew; $focus = $(if ($wn.Primary) { $wn.Primary } else { $form })
  $sec = @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Col -eq 0 }) | Select-Object -First 1
  $res['Scrolls'] = [bool]$main.VerticalScroll.Visible; $res['Before'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y
  $pt = & $wn.ViewMid $sec.Card; $res['Point'] = [string]$pt; $res['PageTop'] = $page.Top
  $t = & $wn.WheelTry $flt $pt $focus -Direct:$Direct
  $res['Under'] = $t.Under; $res['Handled'] = $t.Handled; $res['After'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y
  $g = @(& $wn.Grids | Where-Object { [Pfm.Wheel]::GridCan($_, -120) }) | Select-Object -First 1
  if ($g) {
    $main.ScrollControlIntoView($g); [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
    $res['MainBefore'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y; $res['GridBefore'] = $g.FirstDisplayedScrollingRowIndex
    $t = & $wn.WheelTry $flt (& $wn.ViewMid $g) $focus -Direct:$Direct
    $res['GridUnder'] = $t.Under; $res['GridHandled'] = $t.Handled; $res['GridAfter'] = $g.FirstDisplayedScrollingRowIndex; $res['MainAfter'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y }
  return $res }
$wn.MeasureWheel = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R7 (R32 W2): proves that the mouse wheel scrolls the card from a point on the card, not on the scroll bar, while a
  button has the focus; and the grid under the pointer while that grid can still scroll.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The window is made 60 % as high so that Your Work scrolls; $wn.WheelCase runs twice: straight through the routing
  function on the control tree (Route: no screen pixels, so it holds for this window off the screen), then through the
  window's own filter as Windows calls it (Filter). Then the size comes back and Your Work is shown again. No real
  pointer is moved.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Card, Route and Filter (each a $wn.WheelCase table).
  #>
  $keep = $form.ClientSize; $res = [ordered]@{}; $res['Card'] = 'home'
  try {
    $form.ClientSize = [Drawing.Size]::new($keep.Width, [int]($keep.Height * 0.6))
    $res['Route'] = (& $wn.WheelCase -Direct); $res['Filter'] = (& $wn.WheelCase)
  } finally { $form.ClientSize = $keep; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home'; [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents() }
  return $res }
# The middle of the part of control $C that the main column shows, in client pixels of the window, from the control
# tree (Pfm.Wheel.ClientOf; no screen pixels, so it holds for a window off the screen too). It stops with the places
# when no part shows (R7: an empty overlap gave the point 0,0, on the rail, and hid the cause).
$wn.ViewMid = { param($C)
  $o = [Pfm.Wheel]::ClientOf($C, $form); $mo = [Pfm.Wheel]::ClientOf($main, $form)
  $v = [Drawing.Rectangle]::Intersect((New-Object Drawing.Rectangle($o, $C.Size)), (New-Object Drawing.Rectangle($mo, $main.ClientSize)))
  if ($v.Width -lt 1 -or $v.Height -lt 1) { throw ('no part of ' + $C.GetType().Name + ' at ' + $o + ' ' + $C.Size + ' shows in the main column at ' + $mo + ' ' + $main.ClientSize) }
  return [Drawing.Point]::new(($v.Left + [int]($v.Width / 2)), ($v.Top + [int]($v.Height / 2))) }
# The grids on the page (the card shown), in the order they were built.
$wn.Grids = {
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Queue; $st.Enqueue($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Dequeue().Controls) { if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) { $out.Add($c) } elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Enqueue($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.MeasureRun = {

  .PARAMETER Path

  $form.StartPosition = 'Manual'; $form.ShowInTaskbar = $false; $form.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(-20000, -20000)

  $all = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  & $wn.Build { param($k) try { $all.Add((& $wn.MeasureCard $k)) } catch { $all.Add([ordered]@{ Key = $k; Error = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }) } }

  $res['Client'] = ([string]$form.ClientSize.Width + 'x' + $form.ClientSize.Height)
  $res['Cards'] = $all.ToArray()

  # The rail head and the color choice: a step that cannot be measured is kept as its error (the test names it).

$script:SiteSource = 'fake'; $script:SiteShown = @{}
$script:FakeMarks = @('90161Z TEST', 'XXX XXX ')   # the repo's fake-data markers (see the header)
# The lists this window reads and the columns it reads from each (internal names, schemas/lists).
$script:SiteLists = [ordered]@{
  'PFM Publications' = @('Title', 'PublicationNumber', 'ActionType', 'ProcessStep', 'ActionStatus', 'CoordinationSuspense', 'Modified')
  'PFM Endorsements' = @('Title', 'EndorsementStatus', 'ResponseDate', 'Modified') }
# True when title $Title starts with one of the fake-data markers.
function Test-FakeRow([string]$Title) {
  foreach ($m in $script:FakeMarks) { if (([string]$Title).StartsWith($m)) { return $true } }
  return $false
}
# The number of site rows card $Key shows that have no fake-data marker (0 for a card with no site rows).
function Get-SiteUnmarked([string]$Key) { return @(@($script:SiteShown[$Key]) | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ -and -not (Test-FakeRow $_) }).Count }
# The text of field value $V: a lookup gives its shown value, a date its day as d MMM yy, $null an empty text.
function Get-SiteText($V) {
  if ($null -eq $V) { return '' }
  if ($V -is [datetime]) { return $V.ToLocalTime().ToString('d MMM yy', [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture) }
  if ($V.PSObject.Properties['LookupValue']) { return [string]$V.LookupValue }
  return [string]$V
}
# The weekdays from date $V to today (0 when there is no date): the age of a row on its step.
function Get-SiteAge($V) {
  if (-not ($V -is [datetime])) { return 0 }
  $d = $V.ToLocalTime().Date; $n = 0
  while ($d -lt (Get-Date).Date) { $d = $d.AddDays(1); if ($d.DayOfWeek -ne 'Saturday' -and $d.DayOfWeek -ne 'Sunday') { $n++ } }
  return $n
}
# The chip kind of an Action Status (schemas/lists/PFMPublications.json): On Track ok, On Hold soon, Stalled late, else neutral.
function Get-SiteKind([string]$Status) {
  switch ($Status) { 'On Track' { return 'ok' } 'On Hold' { return 'soon' } 'Stalled' { return 'late' } default { return 'neu' } }
}
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Turns the PFM Publications rows into the row tables of the Your Work grid and of the All Actions grid.
.DESCRIPTION
  The same keys as the cards part's FAKE rows (ConvertTo-HomeRow, ConvertTo-QueueRow): Publication is "number|title"
  (a dash for a row with no number), With is a dash (no person column is read), the row opens the Publications card.
.PARAMETER Items
  The list items (Get-PnPListItem).
.OUTPUTS
  @{ Home = the Your Work rows; Queue = the All Actions rows; Titles = the row titles }.
#>
function ConvertTo-SitePubRow($Items) {
  $hrows = @(); $queue = @(); $titles = @()
  foreach ($it in @($Items)) {
    $t = Get-SiteText $it['Title']; $num = Get-SiteText $it['PublicationNumber']; if (-not $num) { $num = '-' }
    $st = Get-SiteText $it['ActionStatus']; $kind = Get-SiteKind $st; $age = Get-SiteAge $it['Modified']
    $due = Get-SiteText $it['CoordinationSuspense']; if (-not $due) { $due = '-' }
    $act = Get-SiteText $it['ActionType']; $step = Get-SiteText $it['ProcessStep']
    $hrows += @{ Publication = ($num + '|' + $t); Action = $act; Step = $step; With = '-'; Since = (Get-SiteText $it['Modified']); Age = ([string]$age + ' d')
      Due = $due; Status = $st; Kind = $kind; Go = 'pub' }
    $queue += @{ Publication = ($num + '|' + $t); Action = $act; Step = $step; Weekdays = [string]$age; With = '-'; Status = $st; Kind = $kind; Go = 'pub'; Me = $false }
    $titles += $t }
  return @{ Home = $hrows; Queue = $queue; Titles = $titles }
}
# Turns the PFM Endorsements rows into the rows of the answers grid (Office is the row title; no person column is read).
function ConvertTo-SiteAnswerRow($Items) {
  foreach ($it in @($Items)) {
    $a = Get-SiteText $it['EndorsementStatus']; if (-not $a) { $a = 'Not Started' }
    $sig = Get-SiteText $it['ResponseDate']; if (-not $sig) { $sig = '-' }
    $done = ($a -ne 'Not Started')
    @{ Office = (Get-SiteText $it['Title']); Answer = $a; Comments = '-'; Signature = $sig; Status = $(if ($done) { 'Answered' } else { 'Waiting' })
      Kind = $(if ($done) { 'ok' } else { 'neu' }); Go = '' } }
}
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Puts site rows into one grid block of a card, or the empty state when there are none.
.PARAMETER Card
  The card key in $Cards.
.PARAMETER Name
  The grid's Name (its accessible name).
.PARAMETER Rows
  The row tables.
.PARAMETER List
  The list title, for the empty-state line.
.PARAMETER Titles
  The titles of the rows, kept for the marker check of the card's picture.
#>
function Merge-SiteGrid([string]$Card, [string]$Name, $Rows, [string]$List, $Titles) {
  foreach ($col in @($Cards[$Card].Cols)) { foreach ($sec in @($col)) {
      $bl = @($sec.Blocks)
      for ($i = 0; $i -lt $bl.Count; $i++) {
        if ($bl[$i].T -ne 'grid' -or $bl[$i].Name -ne $Name) { continue }
        if (@($Rows).Count) { $bl[$i].Rows = @($Rows) }
        else { $bl[$i] = @{ T = 'p'; Style = 'note'; Text = ('Nothing to show yet: the list ' + $List + ' on your site has no rows.') } }
        if ($sec.Cap -and $sec.Cap -match '^Who Has It Now') { $sec.Cap = 'Who Has It Now ' + $mid + ' ' + @($Rows).Count + ' open actions' } }
      $sec.Blocks = $bl } }
  $script:SiteShown[$Card] = @(@($script:SiteShown[$Card]) + @($Titles) | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })
}
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Reads the PFM lists of the site and fills the cards (the window's source is then "site"); on any failure the cards
  keep their FAKE data (source "fake") and the reason is one SOURCE line.
.DESCRIPTION
  Steps: load PnP.PowerShell, sign in (web login, CAC), read each list of $script:SiteLists, then put the rows into the
  grids of Your Work, the "nothing needs you" card (rows On Track), All Actions and the endorsement answers. Adds the
  SOURCE, READ, WRITES=0 and MARKER lines. Writes nothing on the site.
.PARAMETER Site
  The site address (https://<host>/sites/<name>), or '' when none is set (then the cards keep their FAKE data).
#>
function Invoke-SiteRead([string]$Site) {
  $read = [ordered]@{}
  try {
    if (-not $Site) { throw 'no site address is set in RADE' }
    $mod = @(Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name PnP.PowerShell | Sort-Object Version -Descending)
    if (-not $mod.Count) { throw 'PnP.PowerShell is not on this computer' }
    Write-Host 'NOW Signing in to the site to read the PFM lists (if a sign-in window opens, sign in with your CAC)'
    $null = & { Import-Module PnP.PowerShell -RequiredVersion $mod[0].Version -DisableNameChecking } *>&1
    $null = & { Connect-PnPOnline -Url $Site -UseWebLogin -ErrorAction Stop } *>&1
    foreach ($l in $script:SiteLists.Keys) {
      Write-Host ('NOW Reading the list ' + $l)
      $read[$l] = @(Get-PnPListItem -List $l -Fields $script:SiteLists[$l] -PageSize 500 -ErrorAction Stop) }
    try { $null = & { Disconnect-PnPOnline -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } *>&1 } catch { $null = $_ }
  } catch {
    $why = Hide-Site ([string]$_.Exception.Message) $Site; if ($who) { $why = ConvertTo-Masked $why $who.Secret }
    $lines.Add('SOURCE fake (the site was not read: ' + $why.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(160, $why.Length)) + ')')
    foreach ($l in $read.Keys) { $lines.Add('READ ' + $l + ' rows=' + @($read[$l]).Count) }
    $lines.Add('WRITES=0'); return }
  $pub = ConvertTo-SitePubRow $read['PFM Publications']; $ans = @(ConvertTo-SiteAnswerRow $read['PFM Endorsements'])
  $ok = @($pub.Home | Where-Object { $_.Kind -eq 'ok' })
  Merge-SiteGrid 'home' 'Who has it now' $pub.Home 'PFM Publications' $pub.Titles
  Merge-SiteGrid 'empty' 'Who has it now' $ok 'PFM Publications' @($ok | ForEach-Object { ([string]$_.Publication -split '\|', 2)[1] })
  Merge-SiteGrid 'queue' 'All actions' $pub.Queue 'PFM Publications' $pub.Titles
  Merge-SiteGrid 'waves' 'Wave 1 answers' $ans 'PFM Endorsements' @($ans | ForEach-Object { $_.Office })
  $script:GridQueue = @($pub.Queue)   # the All Actions filter ($wn.Refilter) reads it
  foreach ($b in @($Cards.queue.Cols[0][0].Blocks)) { if ($b.T -eq 'grid') { $b.Count = 'Showing {0} of ' + @($pub.Queue).Count + ' actions, as the site lists them' } }
  $script:SiteSource = 'site'
  $lines.Add('SOURCE site (the PFM lists of your site, read-only; ' + $read.Count + ' lists read)')
  foreach ($l in $read.Keys) { $lines.Add('READ ' + $l + ' rows=' + @($read[$l]).Count) }
  $lines.Add('WRITES=0')
  $all = @($script:SiteShown.Values | ForEach-Object { @($_) }); $bad = @($all | Where-Object { -not (Test-FakeRow $_) })
  $lines.Add('MARKER rows checked=' + $all.Count + ' without a marker=' + $bad.Count + ' (a card with one gets no picture)')
}
'@ }

# ---- File 20 of 29: T21\90161Z-T21-probe-r12.ps1 (from scripts/gov/90161Z-T21-probe-r12.ps1, sha256 d59cec316e63)
$files += @{ Dir = 'T21'; Name = '90161Z-T21-probe-r12.ps1'; Kind = 'text'; Sha = 'd59cec316e63'; Data = @'
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  90-161.Z Task 21 probe, r12 (round R42; the code is the same as r11 of R38). Windows PowerShell 5.1, PnP.PowerShell 1.12.0 (no other module).
.DESCRIPTION
  What it is for: the device side of the T21 probe. R26 settled most of the front-end tests (T2, T3, T5, T6, T7, T9, T10
  passed); R29a proved T4 (a second person writes a row). The 2 probe flows are now flows of the solution "90-161.Z flows"
  (fallback A, the PFM 18 Nov 26: a new solution and a hand-made flow failed in R29a to R32 with "The connections could
  not be loaded"; an upgrade of that solution works): "90161Z T21 Probe Health r6" answers a command row with a result row,
  and "90161Z T21 Probe Button r6" is started by a list view button. Excel is not repeated (R27: no Automate tab).
  This script makes the list and library the tests need, adds the second person to the site's Visitors group (and removes
  the person again), formats the list form and a view, starts the health flow, reads what the people and the flows wrote,
  and removes everything it made. Fake data only (the fake workbook comes from scripts/build_probe_samples.py). Counts,
  status codes and field names only: no names, addresses or text from the tenant.
  WHAT R11 CHANGES (R38; PFM 20 Nov 26): Read prints HEALTH NOT RUN and BUTTON NOT RUN when the round ran no flow step
  (both passed in R36 and R37), so a round that tests only T4 reads clean. The whole set is r12.
  WHAT R10 CHANGED (R36; R35 finding 3): the new part Ask writes T4Asked=yes into the person state file and puts the new
  row form link on the clipboard, before the second person adds a row titled T4a; Read (module read r10) counts T4 only
  then, or when a row by another person is there. The whole set is r10, so the probe loads one revision.
  WHAT R8 CHANGED (PFM 19 Nov 26, F2 B): the new part Office and the test EDITALL prove that a PFM Office member who is not
  a row's author can edit that row on a list set to "edit own rows" (the level T20 r2 gives the group PFM Office, F2 A).
  The part lives in the new module "office"; Read prints the EDITALL line, Clean also takes the person out of PFM Office.
  WHAT R7 CHANGED: (1) the health flow writes its row without the Power Automate Management connector, so HEALTH now tests
  that the flow ran on the SharePoint connection of the solution (it no longer counts flows). (2) View takes the button
  flow's ID from the button-flow-id block of the look module, which scripts/build_flow_solution.py writes at build time
  (the ID is the same on every build); the Export part, its module and the flow ID file are gone. (3) BUTTON counts the
  rows titled BTN-FLOW that the button flow writes. (4) Before each action that takes time a part prints one line
  "NOW <what it does>" for the RADE window; a NOW line is not a result line and is not in the result file.
  WHAT R6 CHANGED: (1) the Clean part no longer prints the Recycle Bin item IDs of the list and the library (R29a finding 7:
  a raw RecycleBinItemId table reached the log). (2) The parts Form and View run the two halves of Look on their own, so the
  round can show the list form when the form header passed, whatever the view result (R29a finding 6); Look still runs both.
  (3) The script is split into modules (code standard, S1): this file holds the start, the shared blocks and the result
  file; the parts live in the files 90161Z-T21-<part>-r12.ps1 in the same folder, which this file loads by name.
  (4) Read: with no state file and no row by another person, T4 is not counted: one line "T4 NOT RUN" and no RESULT line.
  Parts (-Part):
    Make   (about 1 minute, an estimate)  Makes the library "90161Z Probe Files" and the list "90161Z Probe" (columns
           ProbeTest, ProbeWay, ProbeResult, ProbeDetail; its own permissions: the site's copied, then Contribute for the
           site's Visitors group on this list only), saves the fake workbook from a text block in the make module, uploads
           it and writes the test page 90161Z-T21-links-r5.html (4 links). Run it twice and the second run changes nothing.
    Person (about 1 minute, an estimate)  Opens a small window and asks for the e-mail address of the second person (test
           T4). The address stays in memory: it is never written to a file, to the screen or to the results. With your own
           sign-in it adds that person to the site's Visitors group and saves only the number of the site user (no address,
           no name) in the state file 90161Z-T21-person-state-r3.txt in the T21 folder, so that Clean can find the person.
           It also puts the link of the new row form on the clipboard. Prints "added to Visitors: yes" or "no" and a status.
    Office (about 1 minute, an estimate; after Person and after T20 r2)  Sets "edit own rows" on the probe list, gives
           the group PFM Office the level "PFM Office Edit All Items" on it, writes 1 row titled EDITALL (you are its
           author), puts the second person of Person into PFM Office (state file 90161Z-T21-office-state-r8.txt: numbers
           only) and reads back that the person can edit every row. The row's edit form link goes on the clipboard: the
           second person opens it, changes the row and saves it.
    Ask    (a few seconds; no sign-in; after Person)  Writes T4Asked=yes into the state file 90161Z-T21-person-state-r3.txt
           and puts the link of the new row form on the clipboard, for the second person's row T4a.
    Run    (a few seconds, an estimate)  Adds 1 command row (RUN-HEALTH) that starts the health flow "90161Z T21 Probe
           Health r6"; it answers within minutes.
    Look   (about 1 minute, an estimate)  Runs Form, then View.
    Form   (about 1 minute, an estimate)  Sets a header on the list form (the content type's form formatting) and reads it back.
    View   (about 1 minute, an estimate)  Makes the view "ProbeButton" with a button that starts the button flow "90161Z
           T21 Probe Button r6" (a view formatting with the action executeFlow; the flow's ID is in the look module).
    Open   (a few seconds; no sign-in)  Writes the test page again and opens it in the browser.
    Read   (about 1 to 5 minutes, an estimate)  Waits up to -WaitMinutes (default 4) for the health flow's row, then prints
           one line each for HEALTH, T4, EDITALL and BUTTON (counts only; the button flow's rows are the ones titled
           BTN-FLOW). EDITALL passes when the second person saved the EDITALL row that you wrote.
    Clean  (about 1 minute, an estimate)  Removes the second person from the Visitors group and from PFM Office again (found
           by the saved numbers; then deletes the state files), then moves the list and the library to the site Recycle Bin (restorable
           for 93 days). Each step runs even if an earlier one failed, and the part can be run again. The 2 probe flows
           stay in the solution "90-161.Z flows" (the part says so). The round runs it twice: first (-Label first), last
           (-Label last).
  WHAT IT CHANGES ON THE SITE: Make adds the two objects, their columns, their permissions and two files. Person adds one
  person to the Visitors group. Office sets "edit own rows" and the PFM Office level on the probe list, adds 1 row and puts
  that person into PFM Office. Run adds 1 row. Form sets one form formatting; View adds one view. Read, Open and Ask change
  nothing on the site. Clean undoes Person and recycles the two objects. On this computer: the T21 folder (the test
  page, the state file). Every output line shows the site as <SITE> and the DODID as <DODID>; the test page holds the
  site address and stays on this computer (it is not a result file).
  Network: the one SharePoint site given in RADE (RADE_SITE) or in Config\90161Z-site.txt, through PnP.PowerShell; Open
           and Ask use no network (Open hands the test page to the browser).
  Writes: the site objects listed above; on this computer the T21 folder (result files, test page, state files, the fake
          workbook) and, once, Config\90161Z-site.txt when the site address is typed outside RADE.
  Credentials: your own CAC sign-in through the PnP web login window (Connect-PnPOnline -UseWebLogin); nothing is stored.
  Output: 90161Z-T21-probe-<part>-r12.txt (make, person, office, run, look, form, view, read) or -clean-<label>-r12.txt in
  the T21 folder (send them back). Each test line (HEALTH, T4, EDITALL, BUTTON, FORM, VIEW) is followed by "RESULT <test> PASS" or
  "RESULT <test> FAIL", so the RADE step counts what the part read (R28 finding 7). Last line of each part: PROBE <part>
  done: passed=<n> failed=<n>. Exit code 0 when the part ran to its end (a FAILED test is a result); exit 1 only when the
  part could not run (sign-in, missing list, missing module file).
  Run: powershell.exe -NoProfile -File 90161Z-T21-probe-r12.ps1 -Part <part> (RADE does this).
  Parameters (used by RADE, the Redacted Application Deployment Engine): -Id, -Part, -Label, -WaitMinutes, -NoPause.
  -PollSeconds, -TestDir and -NoLaunch are for the tests in tests/run.sh (tests/ps/Test-T21.ps1).
.PARAMETER Id
  The DODID (the profile folder name); empty = the profile folder of this computer.
.PARAMETER Part
  The part to run: Make, Person, Ask, Office, Run, Look, Form, View, Open, Read or Clean.
.PARAMETER Label
  For Clean: first or last (it goes into the result file name).
.PARAMETER WaitMinutes
  How long Read waits for the health flow's row (default 4 for Read).
.PARAMETER NoPause
  No "Press Enter to close" at the end.
.PARAMETER PollSeconds
  Seconds between two checks while Read waits (tests use 1).
.PARAMETER TestDir
  Test runs only: the folder to use instead of the T21 folder.
.PARAMETER NoLaunch
  Test runs only: do not open the browser or use the clipboard.
#>
param([string]$Id, [ValidateSet('Make', 'Person', 'Ask', 'Office', 'Run', 'Look', 'Form', 'View', 'Open', 'Read', 'Clean')][string]$Part,
  [ValidateSet('', 'first', 'last')][string]$Label = '', [double]$WaitMinutes = 14, [switch]$NoPause, [int]$PollSeconds = 20,
  [string]$TestDir, [switch]$NoLaunch)
$task = 'T21'
$script:pollEvery = $PollSeconds
$script:LibTitle = '90161Z Probe Files'
$script:LibFolder = '90161ZProbeFiles'
$script:ListTitle = '90161Z Probe'
$script:ListFolder = '90161ZProbe'
$script:BookName = '90161Z-T21-fake-book-r1.xlsx'
# The test page keeps its r5 name: the round's sample page (samples/90161Z-T21-links-r5.html) has that name, and no check
# ties it to the script revision.
$script:LinksName = '90161Z-T21-links-r5.html'
# The state file keeps its r3 name: Clean finds a person that an earlier round added through it.
$script:StateName = '90161Z-T21-person-state-r3.txt'
# The part Office (F2 B): the group and the level T20 r2 makes (the same names as there; tests/ps/Test-T21.ps1 checks), and
# its own state file for Clean.
$script:OfficeGroup = 'PFM Office'
$script:OfficeLevel = 'PFM Office Edit All Items'
$script:OfficeStateName = '90161Z-T21-office-state-r8.txt'   # keeps r8: same format, so a person an r8 run left is found
$script:ViewTitle = 'ProbeButton'
$script:HeaderText = '90-161.Z test header'
$Rev = 'r12'
# The modules this file loads from its own folder (round skill section 2: scripts that load each other keep fixed names).
$ModuleNames = @('common', 'make', 'person', 'office', 'look', 'read')

# @@SHARED task-common-2b522804@@ (RADE writes the shared block "task-common" here; its text is in the bundle part "Shared blocks")
# @@SHARED site-common-cc1bf548@@ (RADE writes the shared block "site-common" here; its text is in the bundle part "Shared blocks")

$secret = @()
$site = ''
$lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$dir = ''
$passed = 0; $failed = 0
$fatal = $false
$script:fmtError = ''
try {
  $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
  if (-not $Part) { throw 'PART not given: use -Part Make, Person, Ask, Office, Run, Look, Form, View, Open, Read or Clean.' }
  # The modules are dot-sourced here, in this script's scope, so their functions see the values above.
  foreach ($moduleName in $ModuleNames) {
    $moduleFile = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot ('90161Z-T21-' + $moduleName + '-' + $Rev + '.ps1')
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $moduleFile -PathType Leaf)) {
      throw ('MODULE missing: 90161Z-T21-' + $moduleName + '-' + $Rev + '.ps1 is not in the folder of this script. Run the round again.')
    }
    . $moduleFile
  }
  if ($Part -eq 'Read' -and -not $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('WaitMinutes')) { $WaitMinutes = 4 }
  $who = Get-TaskId $Id
  $id = $who.Id
  $secret = $who.Secret
  if ($TestDir) { $dir = $TestDir } else { $dir = Get-TaskDir $id $task 'Task 21' -Create }
  Set-Location -LiteralPath $dir
  $configDir = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $dir) 'Config'
  $site = Get-SiteAddress $configDir
  $lines.Add('TASK T21 probe ' + $Rev + ', part ' + $Part + ', ' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') + $(if ($Part -eq 'Read') { ', wait-minutes=' + $WaitMinutes } else { '' }))

  # Open and Ask work on this computer only; every other part signs in first.
  if ($Part -eq 'Open') { Invoke-OpenPart } elseif ($Part -eq 'Ask') { Invoke-AskPart }
  else {
    Connect-ProbeSite
    switch ($Part) {
      'Make' { Invoke-MakePart }
      'Person' { Invoke-PersonPart }
      'Office' { Invoke-OfficePart }
      'Run' { Invoke-RunPart }
      'Look' { Invoke-FormPart; Invoke-ViewPart }
      'Form' { Invoke-FormPart }
      'View' { Invoke-ViewPart }
      'Read' { Invoke-ReadPart }
      default { Invoke-CleanPart }
    }
    try { $null = & { Disconnect-PnPOnline -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } *>&1 } catch { $null = $_ }
  }
  $lines.Add('PROBE ' + $Part + ' done: passed=' + $passed + ' failed=' + $failed)
} catch {
  $fatal = $true
  $m = ConvertTo-Masked (Hide-Site ([string]$_) $site) $secret
  $lines.Add('STOPPED: ' + $m.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(400, $m.Length)) + ' (a part that stopped can be run again: Make skips what is there, Clean finishes what is left)')
  $lines.Add('PROBE ' + $Part + ' done: passed=' + $passed + ' failed=' + $failed)
} finally {
  # Every line is masked once more before it is shown or saved; Open writes no result file.
  $masked = @($lines | ForEach-Object { ConvertTo-Masked (Hide-Site $_ $site) $secret })
  $resultName = '90161Z-T21-probe-' + ([string]$Part).ToLowerInvariant() + $(if ($Label) { '-' + $Label } else { '' }) + '-' + $Rev + '.txt'
  if ($dir -and $Part -and $Part -ne 'Open') { try { Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $dir $resultName) -Value $masked -Encoding UTF8 } catch { $null = $_ } }
  $masked | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
  if (-not $NoPause -and -not $env:RADE_CONTRACT) { [void](Read-Host 'Press Enter to close') }
}
if ($fatal) { exit 1 }
exit 0
'@ }

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  90-161.Z Task 21 probe r12, module "common": the helpers every part of the probe uses.
.DESCRIPTION
  Loaded by 90161Z-T21-probe-r12.ps1 (dot-sourced from the same folder); it does nothing when it is run alone.
  Inputs: the values the main file sets in its own scope ($site, $dir, $lines, $passed, $failed, $WaitMinutes, $pollEvery,
  $StateName). Outputs: functions for the SharePoint REST calls, the result lines, the NOW lines, the wait loop, the
  second person's saved numbers and the sign-in.

  Writes: none on the site by itself (Invoke-Rest sends what a part asks for); the result lines in memory.
  Credentials: your own CAC sign-in through the PnP web login window (Connect-ProbeSite); nothing is stored.

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Sends one SharePoint REST request through the signed-in PnP connection (the same call T20 uses).
.PARAMETER Method
  Get, Post or Merge.
.PARAMETER Uri
  The address after the site, for example _api/web/lists.
.PARAMETER Body
  The JSON body for Post and Merge (verbose form); empty for Get.
.OUTPUTS
  System.String. The raw answer text.
#>
function Invoke-Rest([string]$Method, [string]$Uri, [string]$Body) {
  $url = $script:site.TrimEnd('/') + '/' + $Uri
  if ($Method -eq 'Get') { return [string](Invoke-PnPSPRestMethod -Method Get -Url $url -Raw -ErrorAction Stop) }
  return [string](Invoke-PnPSPRestMethod -Method $Method -Url $url -Content $Body -ContentType 'application/json;odata=verbose' -Raw -ErrorAction Stop)
}
# Reads a REST collection and returns its "value" items as an array.
function Get-RestValue([string]$Uri) { return @(((Invoke-Rest 'Get' $Uri '') | ConvertFrom-Json).value) }
function Get-SiteList {
  # Every list on the site that is not hidden, with the folder name it was made under (the folder name never changes).
  $select = '$select=Id,Title,ItemCount,BaseTemplate,Hidden,EnableAttachments,HasUniqueRoleAssignments,RootFolder/Name'
  return @(Get-RestValue ('_api/web/lists?' + $select + '&$expand=RootFolder&$top=1000') | Where-Object { -not $_.Hidden })
}
# Finds a list or library by the folder name it was made under; returns it, or $null.
function Find-ByFolder([string]$Folder) {
  foreach ($l in (Get-SiteList)) { if ([string]$l.RootFolder.Name -eq $Folder) { return $l } }
  return $null
}
# Prints one "NOW <text>" line before an action that takes time (the RADE window shows it as it happens). It goes to the
# screen only: it is not a result line, so it is not added to the result lines or the result file and is not counted.
function Write-Now([string]$Text) { Write-Host ('NOW ' + $Text) }
# Adds one "ITEM <name> <status> <text>" line and counts a PASS or a FAIL.
function Add-Item([string]$Name, [string]$Status, [string]$Text) {
  $script:lines.Add('ITEM ' + $Name + ' ' + $Status + $(if ($Text) { ' ' + $Text } else { '' }))
  if ($Status -eq 'PASS') { $script:passed++ } elseif ($Status -eq 'FAIL') { $script:failed++ }
}
function Add-Test([string]$Name, [string[]]$Piece, [bool]$Pass) {
  # One summary line per test: "T4 PASSED: a ...; next ...".
  $script:lines.Add($Name + ' ' + $(if ($Pass) { 'PASSED' } else { 'FAILED' }) + ': ' + ($Piece -join '; '))
  # The runner counts a line as passed or failed only by the separate word PASS or FAIL (R28 finding 7: this part read PASSED
  # while its 3 tests failed), so each test also gets one RESULT line.
  $script:lines.Add('RESULT ' + $Name + ' ' + $(if ($Pass) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }))
  if ($Pass) { $script:passed++ } else { $script:failed++ }
}
function Format-Detail([string]$Text) {
  # The flow's ProbeDetail (or an error text) for a line: one line, anything that looks like an address or a link masked, cut to 160.
  $t = ($Text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
  $t = $t -replace '[^\s"<>|,;()\[\]]+@[^\s"<>|,;()\[\]]+', '<MASKED>'
  $t = $t -replace '[^\s"<>|,;()\[\]]+%40[^\s"<>|,;()\[\]]+', '<MASKED>'
  $t = $t -replace 'https?://\S+', '<MASKED>'
  if ($t.Length -gt 160) { $t = $t.Substring(0, 160) }
  return $t
}
function Get-ListRow([string]$Title, [string[]]$Fields) {
  # Plain rows (Id and the named fields as text); only counts and flags are written from them.
  $rows = @(Get-PnPListItem -List $Title -Fields $Fields -PageSize 500 -ErrorAction Stop)
  return @($rows | ForEach-Object {
    $o = @{ Id = [int]$_.Id; Item = $_ }
    foreach ($f in $Fields) { $o[$f] = [string]$_[$f] }
    $o
  })
}
function Find-Result($Rows, [string]$Test, [string]$Way) {
  # The newest RESULT row for a test and way, or $null.
  $hit = @($Rows | Where-Object { $_.Title -eq 'RESULT' -and $_.ProbeTest -eq $Test -and $_.ProbeWay -eq $Way } | Sort-Object { $_.Id } -Descending)
  if ($hit.Count) { return $hit[0] }
  return $null
}

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Checks every $pollEvery seconds for up to $WaitMinutes (both set by the main file); a NOW line a minute.
.DESCRIPTION
  A failed check is retried; 3 failures in a row stop the part (the error goes to the caller). This one differs from the
  shared Wait-Until of T18 and T24 (scripts/gov/src/wait-common.ps1): it takes its poll time from -PollSeconds, so the tests
  can wait 1 second, and it prints one NOW line a minute.
.PARAMETER Done
  The check: a script block that returns $true when the wait is over.
.PARAMETER What
  What is waited for, for the progress line.
.OUTPUTS
  System.Boolean. $true when the check passed in time, $false when the time ran out.
#>
function Wait-Until([scriptblock]$Done, [string]$What) {
  $start = Get-Date
  $end = $start.AddMinutes($WaitMinutes)
  $misses = 0; $nextNote = $start.AddMinutes(1)
  while ($true) {
    $isDone = $false
    try { $isDone = [bool](& $Done); $misses = 0 }
    catch {
      $misses++
      if ($misses -ge 3) { throw }
      Write-Now ('Checking again (a check failed, ' + $misses + ' of 3 allowed in a row)')
    }
    if ($isDone) { return $true }
    $now = Get-Date
    if ($now -ge $end) { return $false }
    if ($now -ge $nextNote) {
      Write-Now ('Waiting for ' + $What + ' (' + [int]($now - $start).TotalMinutes + ' of ' + $WaitMinutes + ' minutes)')
      $nextNote = $nextNote.AddMinutes(1)
    }
    Start-Sleep -Seconds $pollEvery
  }
}
# The site user number of the author of a row, or 0 when the row has none.
function Get-AuthorId($Row) { $a = $Row.Item['Author']; if ($a -and $a.LookupId) { return [int]$a.LookupId }; return 0 }
# The site user number of the person who saved a row last (Modified By), or 0 when the row has none.
function Get-EditorId($Row) { $a = $Row.Item['Editor']; if ($a -and $a.LookupId) { return [int]$a.LookupId }; return 0 }
# The site user numbers of the members of one site group.
function Get-GroupMemberId([int]$GroupId) {
  return @(Get-RestValue ('_api/web/sitegroups/getbyid(' + $GroupId + ')/users?$select=Id&$top=5000') | ForEach-Object { [int]$_.Id })
}
# The Id of the site's associated Visitors group, or 0 when the site has none or it cannot be read.
function Get-VisitorGroupId {
  try { return [int]((Invoke-Rest 'Get' '_api/web/associatedvisitorgroup?$select=Id' '') | ConvertFrom-Json).Id } catch { return 0 }
}
function Read-State([string]$Dir) {
  # The saved numbers of the second person (site user Id, group Id, whether the person was a member before): no address, no name.
  $f = Join-Path $Dir $StateName
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f -PathType Leaf)) { return $null }
  $h = @{}
  foreach ($l in @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $f)) { if ([string]$l -match '^(\w+)=(.*)$') { $h[$Matches[1]] = $Matches[2].Trim() } }
  if ($h['UserId'] -notmatch '^\d+$') { return $null }
  return $h
}
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Loads PnP.PowerShell, signs in to the site with the web login (CAC) and reads the lists once, so the REST route is
  proved by a read before anything is written. Adds the lines ROUTE and ITEM a-rest-read.
#>
function Connect-ProbeSite {
  Write-Now 'Loading PnP.PowerShell'
  $mod = @(Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name PnP.PowerShell | Sort-Object Version -Descending)
  if (-not $mod.Count) { throw 'PNP not installed: PnP.PowerShell is not on this computer.' }
  $null = & { Import-Module PnP.PowerShell -RequiredVersion $mod[0].Version -DisableNameChecking } *>&1
  Write-Now 'Signing in to the site (if a sign-in window opens, sign in with your CAC)'
  $null = & { Connect-PnPOnline -Url $script:site -UseWebLogin -ErrorAction Stop } *>&1
  $script:lines.Add('ROUTE web-login PASS')
  Write-Now 'Reading the lists of the site'
  $siteLists = Get-SiteList
  $script:lines.Add('ITEM a-rest-read INFO lists read from the site=' + $siteLists.Count)
}
'@ }

# Encodes a text for HTML (the test page).
function Get-HtmlText([string]$Text) { return [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($Text) }

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Writes the test page: one big link per thing to open. Colors and font as the RADE window.
.DESCRIPTION
  The page holds the site address, so it stays in the T21 folder on this computer; it is never a result file.
.PARAMETER Dir
  The T21 folder.
.PARAMETER Site
  The site address.
.OUTPUTS
  System.Int32. The number of links on the page.
#>
function Write-LinksPage([string]$Dir, [string]$Site) {
  $s = $Site.TrimEnd('/')
  $links = @(
    @('Open the new row form', ($s + '/Lists/' + $ListFolder + '/NewForm.aspx'), 'Tests T4 and the list form look: the form other people use.'),
    @('Open the probe list', ($s + '/Lists/' + $ListFolder + '/AllItems.aspx'), 'The rows the tests wrote.'),
    @('Open the list with the button', ($s + '/Lists/' + $ListFolder + '/' + $ViewTitle + '.aspx'), 'The view look: a button that starts a flow.'),
    @('Open the fake workbook', ($s + '/' + $LibFolder + '/' + $BookName + '?web=1'), 'The Excel look: a workbook in Excel for the web.'))
  $body = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
  [void]$body.Append('<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>90-161.Z test page r6</title><style>')
  [void]$body.Append('body{font-family:"Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif;color:#1b2430;background:#fff;margin:0}.light{height:6px;background:#ffd520}')
  [void]$body.Append('main{max-width:760px;padding:24px 32px}h1{font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold","Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif;font-weight:600;')
  [void]$body.Append('font-size:29px;color:#0b2545;margin:8px 0 4px}')
  [void]$body.Append('p{font-size:15px;color:#5a6573;margin:0 0 24px}a.go{display:block;border:1px solid #00539f;background:#00539f;color:#fff;')
  [void]$body.Append('text-decoration:none;font-size:17px;font-weight:700;padding:14px 18px;margin:0 0 4px}')
  [void]$body.Append('a.go:focus{outline:2px solid #0b2545;outline-offset:2px}span.why{display:block;font-size:14px;color:#5a6573;margin:0 0 20px}')
  [void]$body.Append('</style></head><body><div class="light"></div><main>')
  [void]$body.Append('<h1>90-161.Z test page</h1><p>Round R30. Fake data only. Open each link when the RADE window says so.</p>')
  foreach ($l in $links) {
    [void]$body.Append('<a class="go" href="' + (Get-HtmlText $l[1]) + '">' + (Get-HtmlText $l[0]) + '</a><span class="why">' + (Get-HtmlText $l[2]) + '</span>')
  }
  [void]$body.Append('</main></body></html>')
  Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Dir $LinksName) -Value $body.ToString() -Encoding UTF8
  return $links.Count
}

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Make, step m3: the 4 text columns of the probe list (internal name = display name). Adds an ITEM line.
.PARAMETER List
  The probe list (from Find-ByFolder).
.PARAMETER Made
  The counts of what was made (columns is raised here).
.PARAMETER Skip
  The counts of what was there already (columns is raised here).
#>
function Add-ProbeColumn($List, [hashtable]$Made, [hashtable]$Skip) {
  $want = @(@{ Name = 'ProbeTest'; Type = 'Text' }, @{ Name = 'ProbeWay'; Type = 'Text' }, @{ Name = 'ProbeResult'; Type = 'Text' },
    @{ Name = 'ProbeDetail'; Type = 'Note' })
  $have = @(Get-RestValue ("_api/web/lists(guid'" + $List.Id + "')/fields?" + '$select=InternalName&$top=2000') | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.InternalName })
  $bad = 0
  foreach ($c in $want) {
    if ($have -contains $c.Name) { $Skip.columns++; continue }
    $extra = $(if ($c.Type -eq 'Note') { ' RichText="FALSE" NumLines="6"' } else { '' })
    $xml = '<Field Name="' + $c.Name + '" StaticName="' + $c.Name + '" DisplayName="' + $c.Name + '" Required="FALSE" Type="' + $c.Type + '"' + $extra + '></Field>'
    $body = @{ parameters = @{ __metadata = @{ type = 'SP.XmlSchemaFieldCreationInformation' }; SchemaXml = $xml; Options = 24 } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 20 -Compress
    try { $null = Invoke-Rest 'Post' ("_api/web/lists(guid'" + $List.Id + "')/fields/createfieldasxml") $body; $Made.columns++ } catch { $bad++ }
  }
  Add-Item 'm3-columns' $(if ($bad -eq 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) ('columns made=' + $Made.columns + ' already there=' + $Skip.columns + ' refused=' + $bad)
}

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Make, step m4: the list's own permissions: the site's copied, then Contribute for the associated Visitors group on this
  list only. Adds an ITEM line (and a NOTE when the site has no Visitors group).
.PARAMETER Made
  The counts of what was made (permissions is raised for each change).
#>
function Grant-ProbePermission([hashtable]$Made) {
  $lst = Find-ByFolder $ListFolder
  $lbase = "_api/web/lists(guid'" + $lst.Id + "')"
  if (-not $lst.HasUniqueRoleAssignments) {
    $null = Invoke-Rest 'Post' ($lbase + '/breakroleinheritance(copyRoleAssignments=true,clearSubscopes=true)') '{}'
    $Made.permissions++
  }
  $visitorId = Get-VisitorGroupId
  if ($visitorId -le 0) {
    $script:lines.Add('NOTE m4: no associated Visitors group on this site, so Contribute was not added; the T4 test needs a Visitors group')
    Add-Item 'm4-permissions' 'PASS' ('own permissions on the list (copied now=' + $Made.permissions + '); Visitors group not found')
    return
  }
  $contribute = 0
  try { $contribute = [int](Get-RestValue '_api/web/roledefinitions?$filter=RoleTypeKind%20eq%203&$select=Id')[0].Id } catch { $contribute = 0 }
  if ($contribute -le 0) { throw 'ROLE Contribute not found on the site.' }
  $has = $false
  $bindings = $lbase + '/roleassignments/getbyprincipalid(' + $visitorId + ')/roledefinitionbindings?$select=Id'
  try { $has = @(Get-RestValue $bindings | Where-Object { [int]$_.Id -eq $contribute }).Count -gt 0 } catch { $has = $false }
  if (-not $has) {
    $null = Invoke-Rest 'Post' ($lbase + '/roleassignments/addroleassignment(principalid=' + $visitorId + ',roledefid=' + $contribute + ')') '{}'
    $Made.permissions++
  }
  Add-Item 'm4-permissions' 'PASS' ('own permissions on the list, Visitors group has Contribute (changes now=' + $Made.permissions + ')')
}

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Make, step m5: saves the fake workbook from the text block in this module (the repo holds no .xlsx: the personal-data
  scan cannot read a binary file), then uploads it. No macro workbook (PFM 17 Nov 26: endpoint security risk).
.PARAMETER Library
  The probe library (from Find-ByFolder).
.PARAMETER Made
  The counts of what was made (files is raised for an upload).
.PARAMETER Skip
  The counts of what was there already (files is raised when the workbook is in the library).
#>
function Send-FakeWorkbook($Library, [hashtable]$Made, [hashtable]$Skip) {
  $wrote = 0
  foreach ($w in @(, @($BookName, $FakeBookBase64))) {
    $bytes = [Convert]::FromBase64String((([string]$w[1] -split '\s+') -join ''))
    $path = Join-Path $script:dir $w[0]
    $same = $false
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $path -PathType Leaf) {
      $cur = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path)
      $same = ($cur.Length -eq $bytes.Length) -and ([Convert]::ToBase64String($cur) -eq [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes))
    }
    if (-not $same) { [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($path, $bytes); $wrote++ }
  }
  $script:lines.Add('ITEM m5a-workbooks INFO fake workbook saved to the T21 folder now=' + $wrote)
  $filesUri = "_api/web/lists(guid'" + $Library.Id + "')/rootfolder/files?" + '$select=Name&$top=500'
  $inLib = @(Get-RestValue $filesUri | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.Name })
  foreach ($n in @($BookName)) {
    if ($inLib -contains $n) { $Skip.files++; continue }
    $null = Add-PnPFile -Path (Join-Path $script:dir $n) -Folder $LibFolder -ErrorAction Stop
    $Made.files++
  }
  $inLib = @(Get-RestValue $filesUri | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.Name })
  $ok = ($inLib -contains $BookName)
  Add-Item 'm5-files' $(if ($ok) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) ('files in the library: the workbook there=' + $(if ($ok) { 'yes' } else { 'no' }) + ' (uploaded now=' + $Made.files + ')')
}

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  The part Make: the library and the list (m1, m2; the same cmdlet T16 uses for its library), the columns, the
  permissions, the workbook and the test page (m3 to m6), then the MADE and SKIPPED count lines. A second run changes
  nothing on the site.
#>
function Invoke-MakePart {
  $made = @{ library = 0; list = 0; columns = 0; permissions = 0; files = 0 }
  $skip = @{ library = 0; list = 0; columns = 0; permissions = 0; files = 0 }
  Write-Now 'Looking for the library and the list'
  $lib = Find-ByFolder $LibFolder
  if ($lib) { $skip.library++ } else {
    Write-Now ('Making the library ' + $LibTitle)
    $null = New-PnPList -Title $LibTitle -Template DocumentLibrary -Url $LibFolder -ErrorAction Stop
    $made.library++; $lib = Find-ByFolder $LibFolder
  }
  Add-Item 'm1-library' $(if ($lib) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) $(if ($lib) { 'library there (made=' + $made.library + ')' } else { 'library not on the site after the create step' })
  $lst = Find-ByFolder $ListFolder
  if ($lst) { $skip.list++ } else {
    Write-Now ('Making the list ' + $ListTitle)
    $null = New-PnPList -Title $ListTitle -Template GenericList -Url ('Lists/' + $ListFolder) -ErrorAction Stop
    $made.list++; $lst = Find-ByFolder $ListFolder
  }
  Add-Item 'm2-list' $(if ($lst) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) $(if ($lst) { 'list there (made=' + $made.list + ')' } else { 'list not on the site after the create step' })
  if (-not $lib -or -not $lst) { throw 'LIST or library missing after the create step; nothing more was done.' }
  Write-Now 'Adding the 4 columns of the list'
  Add-ProbeColumn $lst $made $skip
  Write-Now 'Setting the permissions of the list'
  Grant-ProbePermission $made
  Write-Now 'Saving and uploading the fake workbook'
  Send-FakeWorkbook $lib $made $skip
  # m6: the test page (it holds the site address: it stays in the T21 folder).
  $n = Write-LinksPage $script:dir $script:site
  Add-Item 'm6-page' 'PASS' ('test page in the T21 folder, links=' + $n)
  $script:lines.Add('MADE library=' + $made.library + ' list=' + $made.list + ' columns=' + $made.columns + ' permission changes=' + $made.permissions + ' files=' + $made.files)
  $script:lines.Add('SKIPPED (already there) library=' + $skip.library + ' list=' + $skip.list + ' columns=' + $skip.columns + ' files=' + $skip.files)
}

}
